docs.title: 🎮 OpenArcade: Social Decision Making for AI Societies
docs.text: OpenArcade is a framework for computational social choice in Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) and the Internet of Agents (IoA). It provides the mechanisms for shaping the composition and behavior of agent populations over time, enabling collective decision-making, coordination, and governance in large-scale, distributed agent societies.

docs.title: 🌍 Vision
docs.text:
In human societies, collective decision-making is central to governance, resource allocation, and conflict resolution. OpenArcade brings this principle into machine-executable, scalable, and verifiable systems, ensuring that autonomous agents can cooperate, deliberate, and decide without central control.

OpenArcade becomes the political layer of MAS and IoA, defining how:

  • 🗳️ Group decisions on tasks, resources are made
  • 🔄 Norms evolve
  • 📜 Governance policies are formed
  • ⚖️ Conflicts are resolved
  • 🎯 Collective objectives emerge from diverse agent preferences

OpenArcade provides formal methods for moving from many inputs to one outcome. Whether the input is preferences, judgments, or proposals, each method defines how agents interact and how the final decision is produced.

docs.title: 🧭 Core Principles
docs.text:
• 📥 Structured Input Gathering Ensure all relevant perspectives are captured, validated, and made interpretable across heterogeneous agents.

  • ⚖️ Equitable Decision Formation Balance fairness, efficiency, and robustness while resisting manipulation.

  • ✅ Accountable Execution Translate collective outcomes into coordinated action, enforce compliance, and monitor real-world impact.

  • 🔧 Adaptive Governance Continuously evolve rules, norms, and protocols alongside the agent population and environment.

docs.title: 🏗️ Framework Overview
docs.text:
OpenArcade implements decision-making strategies as interchangeable building blocks in MAS decision architectures.

  • A system could use: 💬 Discussion → 🧠 Argumentation ↔ 🗳️ Voting ↔ 🤝 Consensus Building as sequential strategies depending on context and requirements.

These strategies span the full lifecycle of collective choice:

docs.title: 1️⃣ Pre-Decision Strategies - Structuring Inputs
docs.text:
Gathering and structuring information, facilitating dialogue, and aligning on problem definitions

  • 💬 Deliberation protocols
  • 🧠 Argumentation frameworks
  • 📊 Judgment aggregation
  • 🗨️ Collaborative Discussion
  • 🤝 Negotiation

docs.title: 2️⃣  Decision Strategies - Collective Choice Formation
docs.text:
Aggregating inputs, applying choice mechanisms, and producing final outcomes

  • 📊 Preference aggregation
  • 🗳️ Voting
  • 🔗 Matching & Assignment
  • ⚖️ Fair division
  • 👥 Coalition formation
  • ⚖️ Weighted Decision-Making
  • 📐 Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM)
  • 🤝 Consensus Building

docs.title: 3️⃣ Post-Decision Strategies - Execution & Adaptation
docs.text:
Enforcing agreements, adapting norms, and refining governance models based on outcomes

  • 📜 Norm & Policy evolution
  • 🌐 Distributed Agreement

docs.title: Why OpenArcade?
docs.text:
Without formalized decision frameworks, MAS and IoA risk:

  • Gridlock – agents unable to agree on a course of action
  • Fragmentation – splintering into incompatible sub-networks
  • Domination – manipulation by powerful or strategic actors

OpenArcade prevents these outcomes by embedding computable, transparent, and fair governance protocols into the fabric of agent societies.

docs.title: 🤖 From Autonomy to Collective Intelligence
docs.text:
MAS and IoA represent a shift from isolated intelligence to networked intelligence. OpenArcade operationalizes this by embedding computational social choice into the infrastructure of agent societies - enabling billions of agents to cooperate, deliberate, and evolve shared governance at planetary scale.

A modular backend for orchestrating structured bidding, social voting, and task delegation workflows. DSL-configurable, event-driven, and designed for distributed multi-agent systems.

docs.title: Bidding System (Orcade)
docs.text:
Orcade is a bidding orchestration service. A creator publishes a bid job to a fixed set of eligible subjects (agents), each subject submits a bid, and once every eligible subject has bid, a pluggable evaluator function picks a winner. All communication with subjects happens through an external delegate system, and all decision logic (qualification checks, evaluation) is delegated to functions hosted in an external function registry — Orcade itself only orchestrates state and timing.

Source of truth for everything in this documentation set:

File Responsibility core/schema.py BidJob, Bid, BidTaskResult dataclasses core/db.py MongoDB persistence for the three collections above core/bidding.py BiddingService — the orchestration logic core/apis.py Flask REST API (app, mounted via main.py / run_server()) core/functions.py FunctionCaller — thin wrapper for invoking PQT/evaluator functions core/agents_functions/ Low-level client for the function registry (AgentFunctions, FunctionsRegistryClient, FunctionCaller) core/subject_task.py SubjectTask — client for the delegate system

docs.title: 1.1 Actors
docs.text:
• Creator (bid_job_creator_id) — whoever opens the bid job. Not otherwise validated or used by the service; it's stored as metadata on the job.
  • Subjects (bid_job_subject_ids) — the roster of agents taking part in a job. In closed mode this is a fixed list decided at creation time, and it is required to bid. In open mode it starts empty and grows as subjects apply (see §1.3).
  • PQT function (bid_job_pqt_id) — "pre-qualification test" function. Optional. If set, it is invoked synchronously for every incoming bid and can accept or reject it before it is persisted.
  • Evaluator function (bid_job_evaluator_id) — required. Invoked exactly once per job, after every eligible subject has submitted a bid. It picks the winning subject.
  • Tie-breaker (bid_job_tie_id) — reserved field, stored on the job and accepted by the API/schema, but not currently invoked anywhere in BiddingService. It exists for a future extension (e.g. calling a tie-break function when the evaluator can't produce a single winner). Today it is inert — treat it as forward-compatible schema, not active behavior.
  • Delegate system (SUBJECT_DELEGATE_URL) — an external service that knows how to reach a live subject/agent and get a response back. Orcade never talks to a subject directly; it always goes through the delegate's submit-and-wait endpoint (see §5).
  • Function registry (FUNCTION_REGISTRY_URL) — an external service that stores callable "functions" (PQT / evaluator implementations) and knows how to run them (stateless job, stateful deployment, or an external HTTP endpoint). Orcade resolves bid_job_pqt_id / bid_job_evaluator_id against this registry and invokes them (see §4).

docs.title: 1.2 Lifecycle of a bid job
docs.text:
1. POST /bid-jobs                         creator opens a job for a fixed
                                            list of subject_ids
         │
         ▼
 2. BiddingService.create_bid_job          job persisted in MongoDB;
         │                                 one background thread per
         │                                 subject fires a "bid_request"
         │                                 task to the delegate system
         ▼
 3. Each subject, asynchronously,
    submits its bid:
    POST /bid-jobs/{id}/bids
         │
         ▼
 4. BiddingService.submit_bid              - checks subject is eligible
         │                                 - (optional) calls the PQT
         │                                   function; rejects the bid on
         │                                   a negative verdict
         │                                 - persists the bid
         ▼
 5. After each bid, the service checks     once bids exist for ALL
    whether every eligible subject has     required subject_ids →
    now bid                                trigger evaluation
         │
         ▼
 6. BiddingService._evaluate (background   calls the evaluator function
    thread)                                with the job + all bids;
         │                                 reads back winner_subject_id,
         │                                 status, result_data
         ▼
 7. Winning bid flagged `is_winner=True`   a "bid_winner" task is sent to
    in MongoDB                             the winning subject via the
         │                                 delegate system
         ▼
 8. Every delegate round-trip (both        stored as a BidTaskResult,
    "bid_request" and "bid_winner")        queryable via
                                            /bid-jobs/{id}/task-results

Key behavioral notes:

  • Closed-mode evaluation is bid-driven, not time-driven. There is no deadline/timer. The evaluator only runs once bids exist from every subject in bid_job_subject_ids. If even one eligible subject never bids, the job simply never evaluates. (Open mode closes on a limit instead; see §1.3.)
  • Notifications and evaluation are asynchronous. create_bid_job and submit_bid return to the HTTP caller immediately; the delegate calls for bid_request/bid_winner and the evaluator call all run on background daemon threads. A client cannot assume a bid request or winner notification has already been delivered just because the HTTP call returned.
  • PQT rejection is synchronous and blocking. Unlike notifications, the PQT function call happens inline inside submit_bid — the HTTP caller gets an immediate accept/reject.
  • The delegate's response is not interpreted by Orcade's logic. Whatever JSON the delegate returns for a bid_request or bid_winner task is stored verbatim as a BidTaskResult for audit/history purposes; it does not feed back into who wins or whether a bid is accepted.

docs.title: 1.3 Bidding modes
docs.text: Every job has a bid_job_mode: closed (the default), open, or mixed.

docs.title: Closed mode
docs.text: The creator names the eligible subjects up front in bid_job_subject_ids. Only those subjects may bid. Each is notified with a bid_request on creation. Evaluation runs once every listed subject has bid. Lifecycle steps 1–8 in §1.2 describe this mode.

docs.title: Open mode
docs.text:
No subjects are named. Any subject may apply, and applying is submitting a bid. The job closes when its limit is reached, and the set of applicants at that moment is evaluated.

  • Limits. Specify bid_job_max_subjects (maximum number of accepted applicants), bid_job_max_time (seconds from creation), or both. If both are set, the job closes on whichever is reached first. At least one is required.
  • Applying. A subject submits POST /bid-jobs/{id}/bids as usual. The PQT function, if configured, runs first. If it accepts, the bid is stored and the subject is appended to bid_job_subject_ids. If it rejects, the subject is not added and nothing is stored.
  • Refusals. An application is refused with 409 if the job is closed, past its deadline, already full, or the subject has already applied.
  • Closing. Closing happens on whichever comes first:
  • the application that fills the last slot (max_subjects), or
  • a background watcher that notices bid_job_closes_at has passed (default poll interval 5 seconds, configurable via BID_EXPIRY_INTERVAL_SECONDS).

Closing is atomic, so the evaluator runs at most once per job. - Empty close. If the job closes with no applicants, it is marked closed and no evaluation runs. - No broadcast. Open jobs send no bid_request notifications, since there is no fixed roster to notify. Subjects discover open jobs themselves, for example by querying POST /bid-jobs/query with {"bid_job_mode": "open", "bid_job_status": "open"}.

Open-mode request and response details are in §3.2.

docs.title: Mixed mode
docs.text:
The creator names the eligible subjects up front, exactly like closed mode: same required, non-empty bid_job_subject_ids, same bid_request notification to each one on creation, same rule that evaluation runs once every listed subject has bid. bid_job_max_subjects and bid_job_max_time do not apply, since the roster is fixed at creation and nobody joins later.

The difference is tagging. For every subject in bid_job_subject_ids, the job is automatically tagged subject::<subject_id> (see SUBJECT_TAG_PREFIX), alongside whatever tags the creator supplied. A subject can then find a job that names it with an ordinary tag search or poll, via GET /bid-jobs/by-tags or BidTagQuery — without depending on the bid_request notification reaching it. This is the "mixed" part: a fixed, closed roster (like closed mode) that is also discoverable by tag (like open mode).

For example, creating a mixed-mode job with bid_job_subject_ids: ["agent-translator-01", "agent-translator-02"] and bid_job_tags: ["translation"] produces a stored bid_job_tags of ["translation", "subject::agent-translator-01", "subject::agent-translator-02"]. If a subject tag duplicates one already in the creator's list, it is not added twice (§2.1 tag normalization still applies).

Bidding mechanics (eligibility, one bid per subject, PQT, evaluation) are otherwise identical to closed mode. Mixed-mode request details are in §3.2.

docs.title: 2. Schema
docs.text: All three entities are plain dataclasses (core/schema.py) that round-trip through to_dict() / from_dict() and are stored as-is (no ORM/mapping layer) as MongoDB documents.

docs.title: 2.1 BidJob
docs.text:
Represents a task that is open for bidding.

Field Type Required Description bid_job_id string (UUID4) auto Primary key. Generated server-side if omitted. bid_job_metadata object yes (may be {}) Free-form metadata about the job (e.g. deadlines, tags, source system). Not interpreted by Orcade; passed through to the PQT/evaluator functions and to subjects. bid_job_description object yes (may be {}) The actual task/work description a subject needs in order to construct a bid. Free-form — its shape is a contract between the creator and the subjects, not something Orcade validates. bid_job_name object yes (may be {}) Human-readable name/label for the job. Modeled as an object (not a plain string) so it can carry i18n variants or structured naming — e.g. {"en": "..."}. bid_job_evaluator_id string yes function_id in the function registry that will be invoked once all subjects have bid. See §4.3. bid_job_pqt_id string no ("" = disabled) function_id of the pre-qualification-test function invoked on every incoming bid. Empty string disables PQT checks entirely — bids are accepted unconditionally. See §4.2. bid_job_tie_id string stored, unused Reserved for a future tie-breaker function. Accepted and persisted, never invoked today. bid_job_creator_id string yes Identifier of whoever created the job. Not validated against any user/subject registry. bid_job_subject_ids array<string> closed: yes · open: no ([] at creation) Closed mode: the fixed list of eligible, required subject IDs. Determines who gets a bid_request and when evaluation fires. Open mode: the roster of applicants, filled in by the service as PQT-passing subjects apply. Must not be supplied on creation of an open job. bid_job_mode string no (default "closed") "closed" or "open". Selects the bidding mode; see §1.3. bid_job_max_subjects integer ≥ 1 open: at least one of this or bid_job_max_time · closed: must be omitted Maximum number of accepted applicants. The job closes as soon as this many subjects have been accepted. bid_job_max_time integer ≥ 1 open: at least one of this or bid_job_max_subjects · closed: must be omitted Duration in seconds, measured from creation. The job closes once it passes. bid_job_status string auto ("open") "open" or "closed". Only meaningful in open mode. Flipped to "closed" atomically by whichever closing trigger fires first. bid_job_created_time datetime (ISO-8601 UTC string) auto When the job was created. Always stored in UTC with microsecond precision. bid_job_closes_at datetime (ISO-8601 UTC string) | null auto created_time + bid_job_max_time, or null if no time limit is set. Open mode only. bid_job_tags array<string> no (default []) Free-form labels for categorizing and finding the job, e.g. ["translation", "fr"]. Used by GET /bid-jobs/by-tags. Each tag must be a non-empty string. Surrounding whitespace is stripped and duplicates are removed on creation. Matching is case-sensitive.

Example — full BidJob document (closed mode):

{
  "bid_job_id": "8f14e45f-ceea-4a19-8f6e-8b5a9c1a9f10",
  "bid_job_metadata": {
    "priority": "high",
    "deadline": "2026-09-15T00:00:00Z",
    "source_system": "task-planner"
  },
  "bid_job_description": {
    "task_type": "translate_document",
    "document_url": "https://storage.example.com/docs/report.pdf",
    "source_language": "en",
    "target_language": "fr",
    "word_count": 4200
  },
  "bid_job_name": {
    "en": "Translate Q3 report to French"
  },
  "bid_job_evaluator_id": "lowest-cost-evaluator:1.0-stable",
  "bid_job_pqt_id": "min-confidence-pqt:1.0-stable",
  "bid_job_tie_id": "",
  "bid_job_creator_id": "planner-service",
  "bid_job_subject_ids": [
    "agent-translator-01",
    "agent-translator-02",
    "agent-translator-03"
  ],
  "bid_job_mode": "closed",
  "bid_job_max_subjects": null,
  "bid_job_max_time": null,
  "bid_job_status": "open",
  "bid_job_created_time": "2026-09-09T10:00:00.000000+00:00",
  "bid_job_closes_at": null,
  "bid_job_tags": ["translation", "fr"]
}

Example — full BidJob document (open mode, after two applicants):

{
  "bid_job_id": "c2d7f1a0-4e3b-4f19-9a52-7b8e1d6c0a33",
  "bid_job_metadata": {"source_system": "marketplace"},
  "bid_job_description": {
    "task_type": "translate_document",
    "source_language": "en",
    "target_language": "fr"
  },
  "bid_job_name": {"en": "Open call: translate Q4 handbook"},
  "bid_job_evaluator_id": "lowest-cost-evaluator:1.0-stable",
  "bid_job_pqt_id": "min-confidence-pqt:1.0-stable",
  "bid_job_tie_id": "",
  "bid_job_creator_id": "planner-service",
  "bid_job_subject_ids": ["agent-translator-07", "agent-translator-09"],
  "bid_job_mode": "open",
  "bid_job_max_subjects": 5,
  "bid_job_max_time": 3600,
  "bid_job_status": "open",
  "bid_job_created_time": "2026-10-05T09:00:00.000000+00:00",
  "bid_job_closes_at": "2026-10-05T10:00:00.000000+00:00",
  "bid_job_tags": ["translation", "marketplace"]
}

Here the roster has two entries out of a possible five. The job stays open until either five subjects have applied or 10:00 UTC passes.

docs.title: 2.2 Bid
docs.text:
Represents one subject's bid for a job.

Field Type Required Description bid_id string (UUID4) auto Primary key. bid_job_id string yes FK to BidJob.bid_job_id. Set by the server from the URL path (/bid-jobs/{bid_job_id}/bids), not by the request body. bid_data object yes (may be {}) The actual content of the bid — free-form, defined by whatever the creator/evaluator expect (e.g. price, ETA, confidence score, proposed plan). This is what the PQT function and evaluator function reason over. bid_subject_id string yes Which subject this bid belongs to. In closed mode it must already be a member of the job's bid_job_subject_ids, or the bid is rejected (not persisted). In open mode there is no prior membership check. Instead, a successful application adds the subject to bid_job_subject_ids. In both modes, a subject may hold at most one bid per job. A second submission is refused with 409. submission_time datetime (ISO-8601 string) auto Defaults to server time at construction. is_winner boolean auto (false) Flipped to true by the evaluation step for exactly one bid per job (the one matching winner_subject_id). Never set by the client.

Example — full Bid document:

{
  "bid_id": "3c7c3e2a-2d1a-4e2d-9a3b-6d2f9e6b0d4c",
  "bid_job_id": "8f14e45f-ceea-4a19-8f6e-8b5a9c1a9f10",
  "bid_data": {
    "price_usd": 120.0,
    "eta_hours": 6,
    "confidence": 0.92
  },
  "bid_subject_id": "agent-translator-01",
  "submission_time": "2026-09-09T10:15:32.481203",
  "is_winner": false
}

docs.title: 2.3 BidTaskResult
docs.text:
Audit record of every round-trip through the delegate system (i.e. every bid_request and bid_winner notification and the subject's response to it). See §5.

Field Type Required Description bid_task_result_id string (UUID4) auto Primary key. bid_job_id string yes Which job this notification round-trip belongs to. bid_subject_id string yes Which subject was notified. task_type string yes Either "bid_request" or "bid_winner" (see §5). task_result object yes The raw JSON body returned by the delegate system's /api/submit-and-wait call. Opaque to Orcade — stored verbatim. created_time datetime (ISO-8601 string) auto When the result was recorded.

Example — full BidTaskResult document:

{
  "bid_task_result_id": "a1b2c3d4-5678-4abc-9def-0123456789ab",
  "bid_job_id": "8f14e45f-ceea-4a19-8f6e-8b5a9c1a9f10",
  "bid_subject_id": "agent-translator-01",
  "task_type": "bid_request",
  "task_result": {
    "acknowledged": true,
    "agent_notes": "Received job, computing bid now."
  },
  "created_time": "2026-09-09T10:15:01.001000"
}

docs.title: 2.4 Storage
docs.text:
All three entities live in MongoDB, database assets (MONGO_URL, default mongodb://localhost:27017), one collection each:

Collection Unique index Secondary indexes bid_jobs bid_job_id bid_job_evaluator_id, bid_job_creator_id, compound (bid_job_mode, bid_job_status, bid_job_closes_at) used by the expiry watcher bids bid_id bid_job_id, bid_subject_id, is_winner bid_task_results bid_task_result_id bid_job_id, bid_subject_id

update() and delete() on any of the databases operate by the entity's own UUID field (bid_job_id / bid_id), never by Mongo's internal _id. Every query() call accepts a raw MongoDB filter document — see §3.6.

docs.title: 3. APIs
docs.text: Base path: none (routes are mounted at root). Default port 5000 (run_server() in core/apis.py; overridable via the PORT env var at the WSGI/container level — Flask's dev server itself is hardcoded to 0.0.0.0:5000 in run_server()).

docs.title: 3.1 Response envelope
docs.text:
Every endpoint replies with the same envelope:

// success
{ "ok": true, "data": { ... } }

// failure
{ "ok": false, "error": "human readable message" }

data may be a single object, a list, or omitted entirely (e.g. update responses only return {"modified": <count>}).

docs.title: 3.2 How to create a bid job
docs.text:
POST /bid-jobs

Creates the job, persists it, and (asynchronously, one thread per subject) sends a bid_request task to every ID in bid_job_subject_ids via the delegate system.

Request body:

Field Type Default if omitted bid_job_metadata object {} bid_job_description object {} bid_job_name object {} bid_job_evaluator_id string "" (job will never evaluate) bid_job_pqt_id string "" (no pre-qualification) bid_job_tie_id string "" bid_job_creator_id string "" bid_job_subject_ids array [] bid_job_mode string "closed" ("open" for open-mode) bid_job_max_subjects integer ≥ 1 null bid_job_max_time integer ≥ 1 (seconds) null bid_job_tags array []

Validation (400 on failure):

Mode Rule any bid_job_mode must be "closed" or "open" open bid_job_subject_ids must be empty or omitted open at least one of bid_job_max_subjects / bid_job_max_time must be set open any limit that is set must be a positive integer (booleans are rejected) closed bid_job_max_subjects and bid_job_max_time must be omitted any bid_job_tags must be a list of non-empty strings (400 otherwise)

Open-mode example — no subjects named; closes after five applicants or one hour, whichever comes first:

curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/bid-jobs \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "bid_job_name": {"en": "Open call: translate Q4 handbook"},
    "bid_job_description": {"task_type": "translate_document", "target_language": "fr"},
    "bid_job_evaluator_id": "lowest-cost-evaluator:1.0-stable",
    "bid_job_pqt_id": "min-confidence-pqt:1.0-stable",
    "bid_job_creator_id": "planner-service",
    "bid_job_mode": "open",
    "bid_job_max_subjects": 5,
    "bid_job_max_time": 3600

Response 201 returns the job with bid_job_subject_ids: [], bid_job_status: "open", and bid_job_closes_at set to creation time plus 3600 seconds.

Closed-mode example — fixed roster of two subjects:

curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/bid-jobs \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "bid_job_name": {"en": "Translate Q3 report to French"},
    "bid_job_description": {
      "task_type": "translate_document",
      "document_url": "https://storage.example.com/docs/report.pdf",
      "source_language": "en",
      "target_language": "fr"
    },
    "bid_job_metadata": {"priority": "high"},
    "bid_job_evaluator_id": "lowest-cost-evaluator:1.0-stable",
    "bid_job_pqt_id": "min-confidence-pqt:1.0-stable",
    "bid_job_creator_id": "planner-service",
    "bid_job_subject_ids": ["agent-translator-01", "agent-translator-02"]
  }'

Response 201 Created:

{
  "ok": true,
  "data": {
    "bid_job_id": "8f14e45f-ceea-4a19-8f6e-8b5a9c1a9f10",
    "bid_job_metadata": {"priority": "high"},
    "bid_job_description": { "...": "..." },
    "bid_job_name": {"en": "Translate Q3 report to French"},
    "bid_job_evaluator_id": "lowest-cost-evaluator:1.0-stable",
    "bid_job_pqt_id": "min-confidence-pqt:1.0-stable",
    "bid_job_tie_id": "",
    "bid_job_creator_id": "planner-service",
    "bid_job_subject_ids": ["agent-translator-01", "agent-translator-02"]

Failure modes: 400 if the DB insert fails (RuntimeError), 500 on any other unexpected error.

docs.title: 3.3 How to submit a bid
docs.text:
POST /bid-jobs/{bid_job_id}/bids

curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/bid-jobs/8f14e45f-ceea-4a19-8f6e-8b5a9c1a9f10/bids \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "bid_subject_id": "agent-translator-01",
    "bid_data": {"price_usd": 120.0, "eta_hours": 6, "confidence": 0.92}
  }'

Processing order inside BiddingService.submit_bid (closed mode):

  1. Look up the job. 404 if missing (ValueError containing "not found").
  2. Check bid_subject_id is in bid_job.bid_job_subject_ids. 400 if not.
  3. Check the subject has no existing bid on this job. 409 if it does, so a subject holds at most one bid per job.
  4. If bid_job_pqt_id is set, synchronously call the PQT function with {"bid_job": <job>, "bid": <bid>}. If the response's "accepted" key is falsy, the bid is rejected and never persisted → 409.
  5. Persist the bid. 500 if the DB insert fails.
  6. Check whether every subject in bid_job_subject_ids now has a bid on file; if so, kick off evaluation on a background thread.

Open mode (bid_job_mode: "open") — the same endpoint is an application:

  1. Look up the job. 404 if missing.
  2. Refuse with 409 if the job is not open, its bid_job_closes_at has passed, or the subject is already in bid_job_subject_ids. bid_subject_id is not checked against a roster, since there isn't one.
  3. Run the PQT function as above. A rejection → 409, nothing stored.
  4. Persist the bid.
  5. Atomically claim a slot. In one database write, add the subject to bid_job_subject_ids only if the job is still open, not past its deadline, not already containing the subject, and below bid_job_max_subjects. If that write matches nothing, the job filled or closed in the meantime. The bid from step 4 is deleted and the request gets 409.
  6. If the claim filled the last slot, close the job and evaluate it on a background thread.

The bid is stored before the subject joins the roster, so every subject in bid_job_subject_ids already has a bid on file when evaluation runs.

Open-mode request example:

curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/bid-jobs/c2d7f1a0-4e3b-4f19-9a52-7b8e1d6c0a33/bids \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "bid_subject_id": "agent-translator-11",
    "bid_data": {"price_usd": 110.0, "eta_hours": 8, "confidence": 0.88}
  }'

Success returns 201 with the bid, as below. Subject agent-translator-11 is now in the job's roster. Refusal returns:

{ "ok": false, "error": "Subject 'agent-translator-11' has already applied to job 'c2d7f1a0-4e3b-4f19-9a52-7b8e1d6c0a33'." }

with 409. Other refusal messages are "Bid job '…' is closed.", "Bid job '…' has passed its deadline.", and "Bid job '…' is full or closed.".

Response 201 Created:

{
  "ok": true,
  "data": {
    "bid_id": "3c7c3e2a-2d1a-4e2d-9a3b-6d2f9e6b0d4c",
    "bid_job_id": "8f14e45f-ceea-4a19-8f6e-8b5a9c1a9f10",
    "bid_data": {"price_usd": 120.0, "eta_hours": 6, "confidence": 0.92},
    "bid_subject_id": "agent-translator-01",
    "submission_time": "2026-09-09T10:15:32.481203",
    "is_winner": false
  }
}

Error responses:

Status When 400 bid_subject_id missing from request body, or (closed mode) subject not in the roster 404 bid_job_id does not exist 409 The subject already bid on this job, PQT function rejected the bid ({"accepted": false, ...}), or (open mode) the job is closed, past its deadline, or full 500 DB failure, or unexpected exception 
// 409 example
{ "ok": false, "error": "Bid 'ca11...' rejected by pqt function 'min-confidence-pqt:1.0-stable'." }

Winner selection is not returned synchronously from this call. Poll GET /bid-jobs/{id}/bids (look for "is_winner": true) or GET /bid-jobs/{id}/task-results (look for a "bid_winner" entry), or have the winning subject watch for the bid_winner delegate task itself.

GET /bid-jobs/{bid_job_id}

curl http://localhost:5000/bid-jobs/8f14e45f-ceea-4a19-8f6e-8b5a9c1a9f10

docs.title: 3.4.1 Find bid jobs by tags
docs.text:
GET /bid-jobs/by-tags

Returns every bid job whose bid_job_tags match the requested tags.

Query parameters:

Parameter Required Description tags yes Tags to search for. Give comma-separated values (tags=translation,fr), a repeated parameter (tags=translation&tags=fr), or both. Each tag is trimmed, and empty tags are rejected. match no (default all) all: a job matches only if it carries every requested tag, so the requested tags must be a subset of the job's tags. any: a job matches if it carries at least one requested tag.

Matching is case-sensitive and uses the same normalization as creation. Results are not filtered by mode or status, so open and closed jobs, and jobs in any status, can all match. Add a status check on the client if you only want open jobs.

# jobs tagged with both "translation" and "fr"
curl "http://localhost:5000/bid-jobs/by-tags?tags=translation,fr"

# jobs tagged with "legal" or "finance"
curl "http://localhost:5000/bid-jobs/by-tags?tags=legal,finance&match=any"

Response 200:

{
  "ok": true,
  "data": [
    {
      "bid_job_id": "8f14e45f-ceea-4a19-8f6e-8b5a9c1a9f10",
      "bid_job_name": {"en": "Translate Q3 report to French"},
      "bid_job_tags": ["translation", "fr"],
      "bid_job_mode": "closed",
      "...": "remaining BidJob fields"
    }
  ]
}

No matches returns 200 with "data": [].

Status When 400 tags is missing or blank, a tag is empty, or match is not all or any 500 Unexpected database error

PUT / PATCH /bid-jobs/{bid_job_id}

Body is applied as a MongoDB $set on arbitrary top-level fields — there is no schema validation on update. Typical use: closing off further bids by clearing bid_job_subject_ids, or patching bid_job_metadata.

curl -X PATCH http://localhost:5000/bid-jobs/8f14e45f-ceea-4a19-8f6e-8b5a9c1a9f10 \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"bid_job_metadata": {"priority": "low"}}'

→ 200 { "ok": true, "data": {"modified": 1} }, or 404 if nothing matched (id not found, or the new values equal the old ones — modified_count reflects Mongo's actual write, not existence).

DELETE /bid-jobs/{bid_job_id}

curl -X DELETE http://localhost:5000/bid-jobs/8f14e45f-ceea-4a19-8f6e-8b5a9c1a9f10

→ 200 { "ok": true, "data": {"deleted": 1} }, or 404 if not found.

3.6 Query endpoints
docs.text:
POST /bid-jobs/query, POST /bids/query, and POST /bid-task-results/query (note: task results only expose query, not full CRUD) all take a raw MongoDB filter document as the request body and return a list of matching documents in the same shape as to_dict().

# all bids submitted by a given subject, across all jobs
curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/bids/query \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"bid_subject_id": "agent-translator-01"}'

# the winning bid for a job
curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/bids/query \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"bid_job_id": "8f14e45f-ceea-4a19-8f6e-8b5a9c1a9f10", "is_winner": true}'

# every job a given evaluator function is attached to
curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/bid-jobs/query \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"bid_job_evaluator_id": "lowest-cost-evaluator:1.0-stable"}'

Because the filter is passed straight to collection.find(), any valid Mongo query operator works ($gt, $in, $exists, ...). There is no projection support and no auth/ACL layer — treat these endpoints as internal/trusted-network only.

docs.title: 4. Functions to write (PQT & Evaluator)
docs.text:
PQT and evaluator "functions" are not code inside Orcade. They are entries in an external function registry (FUNCTION_REGISTRY_URL), referenced from a BidJob purely by function_id string (bid_job_pqt_id, bid_job_evaluator_id). Orcade resolves and invokes them through FunctionCaller (core/functions.py) → AgentFunctions (core/agents_functions/__init__.py), which supports three execution modes per FunctionEntry:

  • external (is_external=True) — a plain HTTP POST to external_function_url with external_headers; the response's "data" key (or the whole JSON body if there's no "data" key) is returned. This is the simplest mode to target when writing a new PQT/evaluator — just stand up an HTTP endpoint.
  • stateful (is_stateful=True) — the registry deploys the function as a long-lived service on first use (deployment is cached by function_id for the lifetime of the Orcade process) and subsequent calls hit that deployment.
  • stateless — run once per call as a registry-managed job.

Regardless of mode, every function receives a single JSON object as input and must return a single JSON object as output. Orcade does not retry, validate, or interpret the response beyond the specific keys documented below — malformed responses surface as KeyError/Nones that propagate as 500s (for PQT, inline in the submit_bid request) or as a logged error with no winner ever chosen (for the evaluator, since it runs on a background thread).

docs.title: 4.1 Authoring format: AIOSv1PolicyRule
docs.text:
For stateful and stateless functions, the registry doesn't run arbitrary scripts — it instantiates a fixed class from your function_code and drives it through a fixed contract. Both the PQT function and the evaluator function are written the same way, as a class named exactly AIOSv1PolicyRule:

import logging


class AIOSv1PolicyRule:

    def __init__(self, rule_id, settings, parameters):
        """
        Initializes an AIOSv1PolicyRule instance.

        Args:
            rule_id (str): Unique identifier for the rule.
            settings (dict): Configuration settings for the rule.
            parameters (dict): Parameters defining the rule's behavior.
        """
        self.rule_id = rule_id
        self.settings = settings
        self.parameters = parameters

    def eval(self, parameters, input_data, context):
        logging.info("input: {}".format(input_data))
        # ... decide, transform, return a dict

How each piece maps onto Orcade's bidding flow:

Piece Where it comes from What it holds here rule_id (constructor) Set by the registry to the function's own function_id Same string as bid_job_pqt_id / bid_job_evaluator_id — useful for logging which rule is running. settings / parameters (constructor) The function_settings / function_parameters dicts stored on the FunctionEntry at registration time Static, per-function configuration — e.g. a PQT's minimum confidence threshold, or an evaluator's tie-break weighting. This is where you put tunables; it is not per-bid data. The registry typically instantiates the class once (especially for a stateful deployment) and reuses it across many eval() calls, so treat __init__ as one-time setup. input_data (eval) The input_data dict Orcade builds in BiddingService and passes to FunctionCaller.call(function_id=..., input_data=...) Exactly the PQT input contract (§4.2) or evaluator input contract (§4.3) below — i.e. {"bid_job": ..., "bid": ...} or {"bid_job": ..., "bids": [...]}. parameters (eval) The optional parameters= kwarg on FunctionCaller.call() / AgentFunctions.call() BiddingService never passes this today (it only ever calls with function_id and input_data), so for PQT/evaluator calls this argument arrives empty — read configuration from self.parameters (set in __init__) instead of this per-call parameters argument. context (eval) Injected by the function-execution runtime itself Opaque from Orcade's point of view — its shape is owned by the function platform, not by this service, and nothing in core/bidding.py depends on it. return value (eval) — A plain JSON-serializable dict. This is exactly the response BiddingService reads "accepted" from (PQT) or "winner_subject_id" / "status" / "result_data" from (evaluator).

If the function is instead registered with is_external=True, this class contract doesn't apply — the registry just does a plain HTTP POST of the same input_data JSON to external_function_url and expects a JSON body back (optionally wrapped in a "data" key). Any HTTP service that honors the input/output contracts below works there, in any language — a Flask example for that mode is included alongside each AIOSv1PolicyRule example below.

docs.title: 4.2 PQT (pre-qualification test) function
docs.text:
Purpose: gate-keep an individual bid the moment it's submitted, before it's persisted — e.g. reject bids that are incomplete, out of budget, or from a subject that failed some external eligibility check.

When it's called: inline, synchronously, inside POST /bid-jobs/{id}/bids, once per bid, only if bid_job_pqt_id is non-empty.

Input contract:

{
  "bid_job": { "...": "full BidJob.to_dict()" },
  "bid": { "...": "full Bid.to_dict(), submission_time already serialized to ISO string" }
}

Output contract:

Key Type Required Meaning accepted boolean yes Truthy → bid is persisted normally. Falsy/missing → bid is rejected, submit_bid raises BidRejectedError, HTTP caller gets 409, nothing is written to the bids collection. (anything else) any no Ignored by Orcade today; free to add a reason field for your own logging/debugging, it just won't be surfaced back to the API caller.

Example input (as delivered to the function):

{
  "bid_job": {
    "bid_job_id": "8f14e45f-ceea-4a19-8f6e-8b5a9c1a9f10",
    "bid_job_metadata": {"max_budget_usd": 150},
    "bid_job_description": {"task_type": "translate_document"},
    "bid_job_name": {"en": "Translate Q3 report to French"},
    "bid_job_evaluator_id": "lowest-cost-evaluator:1.0-stable",
    "bid_job_pqt_id": "min-confidence-pqt:1.0-stable",
    "bid_job_tie_id": "",
    "bid_job_creator_id": "planner-service",
    "bid_job_subject_ids": ["agent-translator-01", "agent-translator-02"]
  },
  "bid": {
    "bid_id": "3c7c3e2a-2d1a-4e2d-9a3b-6d2f9e6b0d4c",
    "bid_job_id": "8f14e45f-ceea-4a19-8f6e-8b5a9c1a9f10",
    "bid_data": {"price_usd": 120.0, "eta_hours": 6, "confidence": 0.92},
    "bid_subject_id": "agent-translator-01",
    "submission_time": "2026-09-09T10:15:32.481203",
    "is_winner": false
  }
}

Example output (accept):

{ "accepted": true }

Example output (reject):

{ "accepted": false, "reason": "confidence 0.42 below required minimum 0.70" }

Reference implementation (AIOSv1PolicyRule, for a stateful or stateless function — see §4.1):

import logging


class AIOSv1PolicyRule:

    def __init__(self, rule_id, settings, parameters):
        self.rule_id = rule_id
        self.settings = settings
        self.parameters = parameters

    def eval(self, parameters, input_data, context):
        logging.info("pqt input: {}".format(input_data))

        bid = input_data["bid"]
        confidence = bid.get("bid_data", {}).get("confidence", 0)
        min_confidence = self.settings.get("min_confidence", 0.70)

        if confidence < min_confidence:
            return {
                "accepted": False,
                "reason": f"confidence {confidence} below required minimum {min_confidence}",
            }

        return {"accepted": True}

min_confidence here comes from self.settings, i.e. whatever function_settings was registered for min-confidence-pqt:1.0-stable — change the threshold by updating the registry entry, not the code.

Alternative reference implementation (external HTTP mode, is_external=True — any framework works, this uses Flask):

from flask import Flask, request, jsonify

app = Flask(__name__)
MIN_CONFIDENCE = 0.70

@app.post("/")
def pqt():
    payload = request.get_json()
    bid = payload["bid"]
    confidence = bid["bid_data"].get("confidence", 0)

    if confidence < MIN_CONFIDENCE:
        return jsonify({"data": {
            "accepted": False,
            "reason": f"confidence {confidence} below required minimum {MIN_CONFIDENCE}",
        }})

    return jsonify({"data": {"accepted": True}})

docs.title: 4.3 Evaluator function
docs.text:
Purpose: given the job and the complete set of bids, decide the winner.

When it's called:

  • Closed mode: once per job, on a background thread, the moment the last required subject's bid is persisted. The bids cover every entry in bid_job_subject_ids.
  • Open mode: once per job, on a background thread, when the job closes (last slot filled, or deadline passed). The bids cover the final roster, which is every applicant that passed PQT. The evaluator is not called if there were no applicants.

In open mode, bid_job.bid_job_status is "closed" in the input, because closing happens before evaluation. Closed-mode jobs never change status, so it stays "open". In both modes, bid_job.bid_job_subject_ids is the final roster.

Input contract:

{
  "bid_job": { "...": "full BidJob.to_dict()" },
  "bids": [ { "...": "full Bid.to_dict()" }, "... one per eligible subject" ]
}

Output contract:

Key Type Required Meaning winner_subject_id string yes Must equal the bid_subject_id of exactly one of the bids in the input. If it doesn't match any bid, Orcade logs an error and evaluation ends with no winner set and no notification sent. status string no Free-form status label, logged for observability (e.g. "resolved", "no_valid_bids"). Not otherwise interpreted. result_data object no (defaults to {}) Arbitrary payload forwarded verbatim to the winning subject as part of its bid_winner task (see §5.3). Good place for things like the agreed price, start time, or evaluator rationale.

Example input:

{
  "bid_job": {
    "bid_job_id": "8f14e45f-ceea-4a19-8f6e-8b5a9c1a9f10",
    "bid_job_evaluator_id": "lowest-cost-evaluator:1.0-stable",
    "bid_job_pqt_id": "min-confidence-pqt:1.0-stable",
    "bid_job_subject_ids": ["agent-translator-01", "agent-translator-02"],
    "...": "remaining BidJob fields"
  },
  "bids": [
    {
      "bid_id": "3c7c3e2a-2d1a-4e2d-9a3b-6d2f9e6b0d4c",
      "bid_subject_id": "agent-translator-01",
      "bid_data": {"price_usd": 120.0, "eta_hours": 6, "confidence": 0.92},
      "...": "remaining Bid fields"
    },
    {
      "bid_id": "9d1e2f3a-4b5c-6d7e-8f90-1a2b3c4d5e6f",
      "bid_subject_id": "agent-translator-02",
      "bid_data": {"price_usd": 95.0, "eta_hours": 10, "confidence": 0.81},
      "...": "remaining Bid fields"
    }
  ]
}

Example output:

{
  "winner_subject_id": "agent-translator-02",
  "status": "resolved",
  "result_data": {
    "reason": "lowest price among bids meeting confidence threshold",
    "agreed_price_usd": 95.0,
    "start_by": "2026-09-10T09:00:00Z"
  }
}

Reference implementation (AIOSv1PolicyRule, lowest-price-wins evaluator, for a stateful or stateless function):

import logging


class AIOSv1PolicyRule:

    def __init__(self, rule_id, settings, parameters):
        self.rule_id = rule_id
        self.settings = settings
        self.parameters = parameters

    def eval(self, parameters, input_data, context):
        logging.info("evaluator input: {}".format(input_data))

        bids = input_data["bids"]
        winner = min(bids, key=lambda b: b["bid_data"]["price_usd"])

        return {
            "winner_subject_id": winner["bid_subject_id"],
            "status": "resolved",
            "result_data": {
                "reason": "lowest price",
                "agreed_price_usd": winner["bid_data"]["price_usd"],
            },
        }

Alternative reference implementation (external HTTP mode, is_external=True):

from flask import Flask, request, jsonify

app = Flask(__name__)

@app.post("/")
def evaluate():
    payload = request.get_json()
    bids = payload["bids"]

    winner = min(bids, key=lambda b: b["bid_data"]["price_usd"])

    return jsonify({"data": {
        "winner_subject_id": winner["bid_subject_id"],
        "status": "resolved",
        "result_data": {
            "reason": "lowest price",
            "agreed_price_usd": winner["bid_data"]["price_usd"],
        },
    }})

docs.title: 4.4 Registering a function
docs.text:
Whatever you write must exist in the function registry under a function_id before it's referenced by a BidJob. AgentFunctions.add() (called automatically, lazily, the first time FunctionCaller.call() sees a given function_id) does a GET /functions/{function_id} against FUNCTION_REGISTRY_URL and raises ValueError if nothing is registered — so an unregistered bid_job_evaluator_id/bid_job_pqt_id will fail the first bid submission (for PQT) or fail silently in the background evaluate thread (for the evaluator) rather than at job-creation time. Registering the function itself (setting its function_type, is_external / external_function_url, etc.) is done against the function registry service directly — outside Orcade's own API surface.

docs.title: 5. How input reaches a subject via the delegate system
docs.text: Orcade never talks to a subject/agent directly. Every message to a subject is routed through SubjectTask (core/subject_task.py), a thin client for an external delegate service at SUBJECT_DELEGATE_URL.

docs.title: 5.1 Transport
docs.text:
POST {SUBJECT_DELEGATE_URL}/api/submit-and-wait

{
  "subject_id": "agent-translator-01",
  "session_id": "8f14e45f-ceea-4a19-8f6e-8b5a9c1a9f10",
  "task_id": "3f9c6d2e-1a2b-4c3d-9e8f-7a6b5c4d3e2f",
  "task_data": { "...": "see 5.2 / 5.3" }
}
Field Value in Orcade's usage subject_id the target agent's ID (an entry from bid_job_subject_ids, or the resolved winner) session_id always the bid_job_id — every notification for a given job shares one delegate session task_id a fresh UUID4 per call, generated with uuid4() task_data the payload the subject actually needs to act — see below

The call is a blocking requests.post(...) with a (10, 300) second (connect, read) timeout — Orcade waits up to 5 minutes for the delegate/subject to respond before the call fails. Whatever JSON the delegate responds with is treated as the task's result and is not otherwise parsed by Orcade's own logic (see §5.4).

docs.title: 5.2 bid_request — sent on job creation
docs.text:
Fired once per subject in bid_job_subject_ids, each on its own daemon thread, immediately inside create_bid_job (so it happens concurrently across subjects, and does not block the POST /bid-jobs HTTP response).

Closed mode only. Open-mode jobs are created with an empty roster, so no bid_request is sent. Applicants discover the job by querying for it.

{
  "type": "bid_request",
  "bid_job": { "...": "full BidJob.to_dict()" },
  "bid_job_id": "8f14e45f-ceea-4a19-8f6e-8b5a9c1a9f10"
}

This is the entire payload a subject needs to decide whether/how to bid: the full job object (including bid_job_description, the actual work spec) is inlined — the subject does not need to call back into Orcade to fetch job details.

docs.title: 5.3 bid_winner — sent after evaluation
docs.text:
Fired once, only to the subject whose bid_subject_id matches the evaluator's winner_subject_id, after is_winner has been persisted on the winning bid.

{
  "type": "bid_winner",
  "bid_job_id": "8f14e45f-ceea-4a19-8f6e-8b5a9c1a9f10",
  "result_data": { "...": "the evaluator function's result_data verbatim" }
}

Note this payload is intentionally lean — it does not re-include the full bid_job object (unlike bid_request); the winning subject is expected to already have that context from having received the bid_request and having submitted a bid itself. Everything the evaluator wanted to communicate back (price agreed, start time, rationale, ...) must be put into result_data by the evaluator function (see §4.3).

docs.title: 5.4 What Orcade does with the subject's response
docs.text:
Both bid_request and bid_winner round-trips are recorded identically: the delegate's raw JSON response becomes BidTaskResult.task_result, tagged with the originating task_type ("bid_request" or "bid_winner"), and inserted into the bid_task_results collection (see §2.3). Nothing in BiddingService reads fields back out of these responses — there is no "subject declined the bid_request" or "subject acknowledged winning" branch in the code today. If you need that kind of feedback loop, build it on top of GET /bid-jobs/{id}/task-results (poll/inspect task_result yourself, see §3.7) or extend _notify_subject in core/bidding.py.

If the delegate call raises (timeout, non-2xx, connection error), the error is logged and swallowed — no BidTaskResult is written, and (for bid_request) the affected subject silently never gets notified, while job creation itself still succeeds. There is currently no retry mechanism.

docs.title: 6. Using the Python client library
docs.text:
The client is a single file, client/bidding_client.py. It wraps the bidding REST API (§3) in dataclass inputs and outputs, and adds a background poller for tagged bidding tasks.

It is standalone. The only third-party dependency is requests, and it does not import anything from the server code. Copy the file into your project, or put client/ on PYTHONPATH.

from bidding_client import (
    BiddingClient, BiddingError,
    BidSubmission, BidTagQuery, BidJob, Bid,
)

docs.title: 6.1 Quick reference
docs.text: Function Input Returns Purpose BiddingClient.submit_bid BidSubmission Bid Submit a bid, or apply to an open-mode job BiddingClient.get_bid_job str (job ID) BidJob Query one bidding task by ID BiddingClient.find_bid_jobs_by_tags BidTagQuery List[BidJob] Query all bidding tasks matching the tags BiddingClient.poll_bid_tasks BidTagQuery, listener, interval BidTaskPoller (started) Background poll for tagged tasks; calls listener.on_bidding_task(BidJob)

docs.title: 6.2 Creating the client
docs.text:
client = BiddingClient(
    "http://orcade.internal:5000",   # required, always passed explicitly
    timeout=(5, 30),                 # optional: (connect, read) seconds
    session=None,                    # optional: your own requests.Session
)
  • base_url is required. The client never reads environment variables. Your code decides where the URL comes from.
  • A blank base_url raises ValueError. Omitting it raises TypeError.
  • A trailing slash on base_url is stripped.

docs.title: 6.3 Dataclasses
docs.text: The client accepts and returns these types. Every input is a dataclass, and every output is a dataclass. The bid_job_* field names match the server schema in §2.

docs.title: BidSubmission (input to submit_bid)
docs.text: Field Type Default Notes bid_job_id str required Goes in the URL path, not the body bid_subject_id str required Your subject's ID bid_data dict {} Free-form; the PQT and evaluator functions read it

docs.title: Bid (output of submit_bid)
docs.text: Field Type Notes bid_id str bid_job_id str bid_subject_id str bid_data dict submission_time datetime \| None Parsed from ISO-8601 is_winner bool Becomes True once the job is evaluated

docs.title: BidJob (output of get_bid_job, find_bid_jobs_by_tags, and poller callbacks)
docs.text:
Field Type Default bid_job_id str required bid_job_name dict {} bid_job_description dict {} bid_job_metadata dict {} bid_job_evaluator_id str "" bid_job_pqt_id str "" bid_job_tie_id str "" bid_job_creator_id str "" bid_job_subject_ids List[str] [] bid_job_mode str "closed" ("open" for open-mode jobs) bid_job_max_subjects int \| None None bid_job_max_time int \| None None (seconds) bid_job_status str "open" bid_job_created_time datetime \| None Parsed from ISO-8601 bid_job_closes_at datetime \| None Parsed from ISO-8601 bid_job_tags List[str] []

BidJob.from_dict(d) and job.to_dict() convert to and from the wire format. You need from_dict when you receive a job embedded in another payload, for example the bid_job field of a bid_request task (§7.3).

docs.title: BidTagQuery (input to tag lookups and the poller)
docs.text:
Field Type Default Notes tags List[str] required At least one tag. Each tag must be non-empty and must not contain a comma match str "all" "all": job has every tag. "any": job has at least one

Validation runs when the object is constructed, so bad input raises ValueError immediately, before any network call.

docs.title: 6.4 Submitting a bid
docs.text:
bid = client.submit_bid(BidSubmission(
    bid_job_id="8f14e45f-ceea-4a19-8f6e-8b5a9c1a9f10",
    bid_subject_id="agent-translator-01",
    bid_data={"price_usd": 120.0, "eta_hours": 6, "confidence": 0.92},
))
print(bid.bid_id, bid.is_winner)

For an open-mode job, the same call is an application. The subject is added to the roster if the PQT function accepts the bid (§1.3).

docs.title: 6.5 Querying a bidding task by ID
docs.text:
job = client.get_bid_job("8f14e45f-ceea-4a19-8f6e-8b5a9c1a9f10")
print(job.bid_job_status, job.bid_job_subject_ids)

docs.title: 6.6 Querying bidding tasks by tag
docs.text:
jobs = client.find_bid_jobs_by_tags(BidTagQuery(tags=["translation", "fr"]))
open_jobs = client.find_bid_jobs_by_tags(BidTagQuery(tags=["legal", "finance"], match="any"))

An empty result is []. The search does not filter by status or mode. Filter the returned list yourself if you need only open jobs.

docs.title: 6.7 Polling for tagged bidding tasks
docs.text:
poll_bid_tasks starts a daemon thread and returns a running BidTaskPoller. The thread queries the server every interval_seconds. Each new matching job is passed to listener.on_bidding_task(bid_task_data) as a BidJob.

The listener is any object that has an on_bidding_task method. You don't need to subclass anything.

class TranslationAgent:
    def __init__(self, client: BiddingClient):
        self.client = client

    def on_bidding_task(self, bid_task_data: BidJob) -> None:
        if bid_task_data.bid_job_mode != "open":
            return
        self.client.submit_bid(BidSubmission(
            bid_job_id=bid_task_data.bid_job_id,
            bid_subject_id="agent-translator-01",
            bid_data={"price_usd": 110.0, "confidence": 0.9},
        ))


agent = TranslationAgent(client)
poller = client.poll_bid_tasks(
    BidTagQuery(tags=["translation"], match="any"),
    agent,
    interval_seconds=10,
)

# later, when shutting down:
poller.stop(timeout=5)

docs.title: Poller behavior
docs.text:
Behavior Detail First poll Delivers every matching job that already exists Repeats Each job is delivered at most once per poller Filtering only_open=True (default) skips jobs whose status is not "open". Closed-mode jobs always read "open", so they are still delivered. Pass only_open=False to receive closed open-mode jobs as well Listener errors Logged with the job ID. The job stays marked as delivered, and polling continues Server or network errors Logged. The poll is retried on the next interval Thread The listener runs on the poller thread. A slow listener delays the next poll running True while the thread is alive and stop() has not been called stop(timeout) Signals the thread to exit and waits up to timeout seconds. Does nothing if called from the poller thread poll_once() Runs one poll synchronously and returns how many jobs were delivered. Use it for manual or one-shot polling

To drive polling yourself, build the poller without starting it, then call poll_once() in your own loop:

from bidding_client import BidTaskPoller

poller = BidTaskPoller(client, BidTagQuery(tags=["translation"]), agent, interval_seconds=10)
delivered = poller.poll_once()

docs.title: 6.8 Errors
docs.text:
Every server-side failure, and every failure to reach the server, raises BiddingError.

try:
    client.submit_bid(submission)
except BiddingError as e:
    print(e.status_code, e.message)
status_code Meaning Typical cause 400 Invalid request Subject not in a closed job's roster, blank tags, bad match 404 Not found Unknown bid_job_id 409 Refused PQT rejected the bid; open job is closed, full, past its deadline; subject already applied 500 Server error Database failure or unexpected exception None No HTTP response Connection refused, DNS failure, timeout

str(e) gives "[409] Subject 'x' has already applied to job '…'." or, when there is no status code, the underlying transport message.

The client does not retry. Retry policy belongs to the caller. Retrying a 409 is pointless, since the refusal will repeat.

docs.title: 6.9 Thread safety
docs.text:
BiddingClient wraps a single requests.Session. The poller thread and your own threads must not share one client, because requests.Session is not guaranteed to be thread-safe.

Create one client per thread:

poll_client = BiddingClient(url)   # handed to poll_bid_tasks
task_client = BiddingClient(url)   # used by your request handlers

docs.title: 6.10 Limitations
docs.text:
• Job creation is not in the client. Create jobs through the REST API (§3.2). The client covers the subject side only.
  • Tags may not contain commas. The server splits the query parameter on commas.
  • Poller state is in memory. If the process restarts, the poller redelivers every matching job that is still open. Make your listener idempotent. A repeat bid from the same subject is refused with 409 in both modes, so resubmitting is safe.
  • Seen-job tracking grows with time. The poller stores one job ID per delivered job for its lifetime. This is negligible at normal volumes.
  • Closed-mode jobs look open. Use bid_job_subject_ids and bid_job_mode to tell them apart in your listener.

docs.title: 7. Using the client in the agent SDK
docs.text:
This page shows how an agent built on the agents SDK (services/agents/libs/agents-sdk) uses the bidding client (§6) to take part in bidding. It covers two ways an agent learns about a bidding task:

  1. Delegated tasks: Orcade calls the agent with a bid_request (closed mode) or a bid_winner, through the delegate system (§5).
  2. Polled tasks: the agent polls for tagged open-mode jobs and applies to the ones it wants.

Most agents use one pattern or the other. The worked example in §7.6 uses both.

docs.title: 7.1 How the SDK runs an agent
docs.text:
From the SDK source:

  • An agent is a class with this shape:

python class MyAgent: def __init__(self, subject, context: Context) -> None: ... def on_preprocess(self, task: AgentTask) -> Optional[List[AgentTask]]: ... def on_data(self, task: AgentTask) -> AgentResult: ... def on_event(self, event_name: str, event_data: dict) -> None: ... # optional

  • The file ends with main(MyAgent). main reads SUBJECT_ID, loads the subject from SUBJECT_DB_URL, and builds an AgentExecutor. The executor creates your agent with (subject, context).
  • on_preprocess runs first. Returning None skips the task. Returning [task] sends it to on_data.
  • on_data returns an AgentResult. If it raises, the SDK wraps the exception in an error result. The worker keeps running.
  • Tasks come from a Redis list (REDIS_URL, REDIS_STREAM). A single worker thread reads them with BRPOP and processes one at a time. Anything slow in on_data blocks every task behind it.

What the agent gets from context:

Attribute Source Use for bidding context.subject_id SUBJECT_ID env var This subject's ID. Use it as bid_subject_id context.delegator AGENT_DELEGATE_URL Delegation to other subjects. Not needed for bidding context.p2p_manager Built-in mesh Not needed for bidding

What the agent gets from subject:

Attribute Use for bidding subject.metadata.subject_search_tags Tags to poll with. Tag bidding tasks the same way you tag subjects subject.identity.subject_id Same value as context.subject_id

docs.title: 7.2 Adding the client to the SDK
docs.text:
The client is one file with no dependencies beyond requests, which the SDK already lists in requirements.txt. Copy it into the SDK's core package:

cp services/orcade/client/bidding_client.py \
   services/agents/libs/agents-sdk/core/bidding_client.py

Import it the way the sample agents import the SDK:

from core.bidding_client import BiddingClient, BiddingError, BidJob, BidSubmission, BidTagQuery

If you would rather not copy the file, put services/orcade/client on PYTHONPATH and import bidding_client directly. Copying is preferable when the agent is packaged into a container, because the file then travels with the image.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
The client takes its URL as a constructor argument and never reads the environment. Your agent reads the variable and passes the value in.

Variable Required Read by Purpose ORCADE_URL yes, if the agent bids your agent code Base URL of the Orcade service, e.g. http://orcade-svc.orcade:5000 ORCADE_POLL_SECONDS no (default 10) your agent code Poll interval for tagged open jobs SUBJECT_ID yes SDK Subject identity, used as bid_subject_id SUBJECT_DB_URL yes SDK Where the subject record is loaded from AGENT_DELEGATE_URL yes SDK Required by Context. Raises ValueError if empty REDIS_URL no (default redis://localhost:6379/0) SDK Task queue REDIS_STREAM no (default jobs:inbox) SDK Task queue key

Set ORCADE_URL in the agent's Docker or Kubernetes configuration, next to the other variables.

docs.title: 7.3 Pattern A: responding to delegated bidding tasks
docs.text:
When a closed-mode job is created, Orcade sends each eligible subject a bid_request through the delegate (§5.2). When the job is evaluated, the winner receives a bid_winner (§5.3).

The SDK delivers these to on_data as an AgentTask. Orcade's task_data is what the agent sees in task.job_data:

# task.job_data for a bid_request
{
    "type": "bid_request",
    "bid_job": { "...": "full BidJob dict" },
    "bid_job_id": "8f14e45f-ceea-4a19-8f6e-8b5a9c1a9f10",
}

# task.job_data for a bid_winner
{
    "type": "bid_winner",
    "bid_job_id": "8f14e45f-ceea-4a19-8f6e-8b5a9c1a9f10",
    "result_data": { "...": "the evaluator's result_data" },
}

Verify before relying on this. The SDK reads task.job_data from the Redis message. Orcade posts task_data to the delegate's /api/submit-and-wait. The delegate service is not in this repository, so I could not confirm how it wraps task_data into the Redis message. Confirm that job_data equals task_data with the delegate team before shipping.

Handling a bid_request in on_data:

def on_data(self, task: AgentTask) -> AgentResult:
    kind = task.job_data.get("type")

    if kind == "bid_request":
        job = BidJob.from_dict(task.job_data["bid_job"])
        bid = self._bid(job, client=self._task_client)
        return AgentResult(
            task_id=task.task_id,
            job_output={"bid_id": bid.bid_id} if bid else {"accepted": False},
        )

    if kind == "bid_winner":
        return AgentResult(
            task_id=task.task_id,
            job_output={"acknowledged": True},
        )

    return AgentResult(
        task_id=task.task_id,
        is_error=True,
        error_data={"stage": "on_data", "message": f"unknown task type {kind!r}"},
    )

Submit the bid inside on_data, before returning. Orcade records whatever the delegate returns as a task result (§5.4), but nothing else is confirmed. The bid is not complete until submit_bid returns.

Orcade waits up to 300 seconds for the delegate to respond. Because the Redis worker processes tasks one at a time, keep on_data short.

docs.title: 7.4 Pattern B: polling for open-mode bidding tasks
docs.text:
Open-mode jobs send no bid_request (§1.3). Agents find them by polling for their tags. The poller thread calls the agent's on_bidding_task method, which submits the bid.

poll_client = BiddingClient(os.environ["ORCADE_URL"])
poller = poll_client.poll_bid_tasks(
    BidTagQuery(tags=subject.metadata.subject_search_tags, match="any"),
    self,                     # object with on_bidding_task
    interval_seconds=float(os.getenv("ORCADE_POLL_SECONDS", "10")),
)

The listener method receives a BidJob. For the threading reason in §7.5, use a separate client for submitting from the poller thread:

def on_bidding_task(self, bid_task_data: BidJob) -> None:
    if bid_task_data.bid_job_mode != "open":
        return  # closed-mode jobs are handled through delegated bid_request tasks
    self._bid(bid_task_data, client=self._poll_client)

docs.title: 7.5 Threads and clients
docs.text:
Two threads can submit bids:

  • The Redis worker thread runs on_data for delegated tasks.
  • The poller thread runs on_bidding_task for polled jobs.

Give each thread its own BiddingClient, so they never share a requests.Session (§6.9):

self._task_client = BiddingClient(orcade_url)   # used by on_data
self._poll_client = BiddingClient(orcade_url)   # used by the poller and on_bidding_task

Both clients must be built before the poller starts, because the poller can call on_bidding_task right away.

docs.title: 7.6 Worked example
docs.text:
This is a complete agent file that handles both patterns. Save it as bidding_agent.py next to the SDK's other sample agents. Replace _bid_data with your own pricing logic.

# bidding_agent.py
import logging
import os
from typing import Optional

from core.agent_executor import AgentTask, AgentResult, Context
from core.main import main
from core.bidding_client import (
    BiddingClient, BiddingError, BidJob, BidSubmission, BidTagQuery, Bid,
)

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class BiddingAgent:

    def __init__(self, subject, context: Context) -> None:
        self.subject = subject
        self.context = context
        self.subject_id = context.subject_id

        orcade_url = os.environ["ORCADE_URL"]
        self._task_client = BiddingClient(orcade_url)   # Redis thread
        self._poll_client = BiddingClient(orcade_url)   # poller thread

        # Start polling before __init__ returns. Build every client first.
        tags = list(getattr(getattr(subject, "metadata", None), "subject_search_tags", []) or [])
        self._poller = None
        if tags:
            self._poller = self._poll_client.poll_bid_tasks(
                BidTagQuery(tags=tags, match="any"),
                self,
                interval_seconds=float(os.getenv("ORCADE_POLL_SECONDS", "10")),
            )

    # ---- pattern B: polled open-mode jobs (poller thread) ----

    def on_bidding_task(self, bid_task_data: BidJob) -> None:
        if bid_task_data.bid_job_mode != "open":
            return
        self._bid(bid_task_data, client=self._poll_client)

    # ---- pattern A: delegated tasks (Redis thread) ----

    def on_preprocess(self, task: AgentTask):
        return [task]

    def on_data(self, task: AgentTask) -> AgentResult:
        kind = task.job_data.get("type")
        try:
            if kind == "bid_request":
                job = BidJob.from_dict(task.job_data["bid_job"])
                bid = self._bid(job, client=self._task_client)
                output = {"bid_id": bid.bid_id} if bid else {"accepted": False}
                return AgentResult(task_id=task.task_id, job_output=output)

            if kind == "bid_winner":
                log.info("Won bid job %s", task.job_data.get("bid_job_id"))
                return AgentResult(
                    task_id=task.task_id,
                    job_output={"acknowledged": True},
                )

            return AgentResult(
                task_id=task.task_id,
                is_error=True,
                error_data={"stage": "on_data", "message": f"unknown task type {kind!r}"},
            )
        except Exception as e:
            log.exception("on_data failed for task %s", task.task_id)
            return AgentResult(
                task_id=task.task_id,
                is_error=True,
                error_data={"stage": "on_data", "message": str(e)},
            )

    # ---- shared ----

    def _bid(self, job: BidJob, *, client: BiddingClient) -> Optional[Bid]:
        """Submit this subject's bid. Returns None if Orcade refuses it (409)."""
        try:
            bid = client.submit_bid(BidSubmission(
                bid_job_id=job.bid_job_id,
                bid_subject_id=self.subject_id,
                bid_data=self._bid_data(job),
            ))
            log.info("Bid %s submitted to job %s", bid.bid_id, job.bid_job_id)
            return bid
        except BiddingError as e:
            if e.status_code == 409:
                log.info("Bid refused for job %s: %s", job.bid_job_id, e.message)
                return None
            raise

    def _bid_data(self, job: BidJob) -> dict:
        # Replace with real pricing logic. Keys must match what the job's
        # PQT and evaluator functions expect.
        return {"price_usd": 100.0, "confidence": 0.9}


main(BiddingAgent)

docs.title: Testing without the full stack
docs.text:
on_data can be exercised directly. Build the agent with a fake context and feed it an AgentTask:

from core.agent_executor import AgentTask

class FakeContext:
    subject_id = "agent-translator-01"

agent = BiddingAgent(subject=None, context=FakeContext())   # ORCADE_URL must be set
task = AgentTask(task_id="t-1", job_data={
    "type": "bid_request",
    "bid_job": job_dict,            # a BidJob.to_dict() from a test job
    "bid_job_id": job_dict["bid_job_id"],
})
result = agent.on_data(task)
assert not result.is_error

subject=None works here because the constructor tolerates a missing subject (getattr guards the tag lookup), so no poller starts when no tags are available.

docs.title: 7.7 Operational notes
docs.text:
• Idempotency. Both patterns can reach the same job. A closed-mode job sends bid_request, and the poller may also see it if its tags match and bid_job_mode is "open". The mode check in on_bidding_task prevents that. Restarts also redeliver open jobs to the poller. A repeat application returns 409, which _bid treats as "already bid".
  • Refusals are not errors. A 409 means the job moved on (full, closed, or already applied). _bid returns None, so the agent does not report an error for it.
  • Unexpected bidding errors. A 400 or 404 raises out of _bid. In on_data that becomes an error result. In the poller it is logged by BidTaskPoller.
  • Startup order. __init__ starts the poller, and the poller can call on_bidding_task at once. Set every attribute on_bidding_task uses before the poller starts.
  • Shutdown. The SDK's main stops the Redis worker on SIGINT or SIGTERM, but it does not know about the poller. Stop the poller yourself, for example by registering a signal handler that calls self._poller.stop(timeout=5). Poller threads are daemon threads, so process exit does not wait for them.

docs.title: 7.8 Observations about the SDK
docs.text:
These came up while reading the SDK for this guide. Neither is fixed here.

  • AgentDelegator.close() in core/delegate.py refers to self.session, but the constructor never sets it, so calling close() raises AttributeError. It does not affect bidding because nothing calls close() today.
  • core/input_streams/redis_listener.py is a separate, generic BRPOP worker. The live path is start_redis_listener in core/utils.py, which the bidding flow relies on.

docs.title: Social Choice Voting System
docs.text:
The voting system runs structured social-choice votes. A creator submits a social task that describes what is being decided and lists the voting options. At its scheduled time the task starts and invitations go out. Voters submit votes, each vote passes a pre-qualification test (PQT), and once enough qualified votes are in, an evaluation job runs the choice evaluation, an optional tie-breaker, and a post-award step. It then stores a report and notifies the winners.

All decision logic (invitation content, vote qualification, counting, tie resolution, post-award actions) lives in pluggable workflows and functions hosted in an external DSL workflow registry or function registry. The voting services handle state, timing, and message delivery.

The system is four services that share one MongoDB database:

Service Source Port Responsibility Submission submission/ 5000 Task creation API, cron scheduler, voting invitations Vote intake votes_submission/ 8081 (REST), NATS vote.submit Vote validation, PQT, evaluation trigger Evaluator job evaluator_job/ — (Kubernetes Job) Choice evaluation, tie-breaker, post-award, report, result notifications Query system query_system/ 8082 (REST), 8765 (WebSocket) Reports, status, task bundles, live streaming

Source of truth for everything in this documentation set (paths relative to services/social_choice/):

File Responsibility submission/core/schema.py SocialTaskCoreData, SocialChoiceSubjectSpecInput, SocialChoiceEvaluationInput, Votes dataclasses submission/core/submission.py SubmissionParser, SocialTaskController: request parsing and task creation submission/core/api.py Flask API for task creation and parsing submission/core/scheduler.py CronScheduler: finds scheduled tasks that are due submission/core/votes_request.py VotingTaskInitiator: starts tasks and publishes invitations submission/core/evaluators/ execute_functionality: runs a function-registry function or a DSL workflow votes_submission/core/servers.py REST and NATS vote intake (VoteServers) votes_submission/core/vote_pre_check.py VotingInitialChecker, VoteAcceptor: validation and PQT votes_submission/core/votes_initiator.py VotingEvaluationInitiator: evaluation trigger and Kubernetes Job launch evaluator_job/core/dsl_flow_executor.py DSLEvaluator: choice evaluation, tie-breaker, post-award evaluator_job/core/finalizer.py VoteResultFinalizer, ResultNotifier: report and NATS notifications query_system/core/queries.py QueriesManager: read-side queries query_system/core/servers.py Query REST API and WebSocket live stream

Implementation status. Some parts of the code do not yet work end to end. The main reason is that the vote-intake and evaluator services still use an older version of the schema. §1.5 lists each gap and its effect. Read it before you deploy.

  3. APIs: REST reference for creating tasks, submitting votes, and querying, plus the WebSocket live stream
  4. Functions to write: contracts for the invitation, PQT, choice evaluation, tie-breaker, and post-award hooks, with reference implementations
  5. Messaging: how invitations reach subjects, how votes arrive over NATS, and how results are announced
  6. Using the system from Python: copy-paste helpers for every API, subscription, and the live stream
  7. Using the system in the agent SDK: wiring voting into an agents-sdk agent, with a worked example
