docs.title: 1.1 Actors
docs.text:
• Creator (created_by_subject_id): whoever submits the social task. Stored as metadata. It is also used as sender_subject_id on invitations (§5.2). It is not checked against any subject registry.
  • Voters: subjects that submit votes. In private tasks only the subjects listed in org_ids may vote. In public tasks any subject may vote. See §1.3.
  • Voting options (voting_options_map): the choices being voted on, keyed by option ID. The system also uses each option key as an address: invitations go to one channel per option key, and result notifications go to each winner ID. In practice, then, option keys are subject IDs, that is, the candidates. See §5.
  • Invitation creator (voting_message_request_creator): optional. A function or DSL workflow that builds custom content for the invitation message when the task starts. See §4.2.
  • PQT (voting_pqt): the pre-qualification test. It runs once for every incoming vote and decides whether the vote is qualified. A disqualified vote is still stored, but evaluation ignores it. See §4.3.
  • Choice evaluation (choice_evaluation): required. It runs once per task, inside the evaluator job, over all qualified votes, and returns one winner or several. See §4.4.
  • Tie-breaker (tie_breaker): optional. It runs only when choice evaluation returns more than one winner. Unlike the bidding system's bid_job_tie_id, this hook is active. See §4.5.
  • Post-award (post_awarding): required. It runs after the winners are final. Its output is stored in the report and sent with the result notification. See §4.6.
  • Constraints (constraints_entry_id, constraints_entry_id_1) and supported protocols (supported_protocols): stored on the task but not read by any service today. Treat them as forward-compatible schema.
  • Function registry (FUNCTIONS_REGISTRY_URL) and DSL workflow registry (DSL_WORKFLOW_URL, WORKFLOWS_API_URL): external services that host the hook logic. See §4.1.
  • Messaging: Redis pub/sub (ORG_REDIS_URL) carries invitations. NATS (ORG_NATS_URL) carries incoming votes and result notifications. See §5.
  • Kubernetes: each evaluation runs as a one-off Job in the votes-evaluation namespace.

docs.title: 1.2 Lifecycle of a social task
docs.text:
1. POST /submit-social-choice-task        creator submits task, subject
         │                                  spec, and evaluation spec
         ▼
 2. SocialTaskController                   three documents persisted in
         │                                 MongoDB under one generated
         │                                 social_task_id; status is
         │                                 whatever the request supplied
         ▼
 3. CronScheduler (every 60 s)             finds tasks with
         │                                 status == "scheduled" and
         │                                 scheduled_time <= now (UTC)
         ▼
 4. VotingTaskInitiator                    - (optional) runs the
         │                                   invitation creator
         │                                 - publishes a "voting_invite"
         │                                   on Redis, one channel per
         │                                   voting option key
         │                                 - sets status = "started"
         ▼
 5. Each voter, asynchronously,
    submits a vote:
    POST /submit-vote  or  NATS vote.submit
         │
         ▼
 6. VoteAcceptor                           - rejects duplicates, unknown
         │                                   tasks, tasks not "started",
         │                                   and (private) non-members
         │                                 - runs the PQT → qualified
         │                                 - checks whether evaluation
         │                                   should start
         │                                 - persists the vote
         ▼
 7. VotingEvaluationInitiator              private: every org_id has a
         │                                 qualified vote
         │                                 public: qualified votes
         │                                 >= duration (default 5)
         │                                 → launch Kubernetes Job
         ▼
 8. Evaluator job                          choice evaluation →
         │                                 (tie-breaker if > 1 winner) →
         │                                 post-award
         ▼
 9. VoteResultFinalizer                    report_json stored,
         │                                 status = "complete"
         ▼
10. ResultNotifier                         "voting_result" published on
                                            NATS, one subject per winner

Key behavioral notes:

  • Start is time-driven. Evaluation is vote-driven. The scheduler starts a task once scheduled_time has passed. After that, no timer runs. Evaluation fires only when the vote threshold is met. A task that never gets enough qualified votes stays "started" indefinitely.
  • The scheduler polls once a minute. A task starts up to 60 seconds after its scheduled_time.
  • Disqualified votes still count as "voted". The duplicate check looks at every stored vote, qualified or not. A subject whose vote fails the PQT cannot vote again on that task.
  • PQT failures disqualify the vote. If the PQT workflow raises, or if launching the evaluation job raises, the vote is stored with qualified = false. Neither failure is reported to the voter.
  • Voting stays open during evaluation. Status changes to "complete" only when the evaluator job finishes. Until then, new votes are still accepted, but the job that is already running does not see them.
  • Messages are fire-and-forget. Invitations use Redis pub/sub, so a subject that is not subscribed when the task starts never receives its invitation. Result notifications on NATS have the same property. The system keeps no delivery record. Compare the bidding system's BidTaskResult.

docs.title: 1.3 Access modes
docs.text: Every task has a social_task_access_type of "private" or "public".

docs.title: Private
docs.text: The creator names the eligible voters up front in org_ids. A vote from any other subject is rejected. Evaluation starts once every subject in org_ids has a qualified vote on file. If even one listed voter never votes, or that voter's vote is disqualified, the task never evaluates.

docs.title: Public
docs.text:
Any subject may vote. org_ids is not checked. Evaluation starts once the number of qualified votes reaches duration, or 5 if duration is not set.

duration is a vote count, not a time span. The name is historical. No service treats it as seconds.

Any other value of social_task_access_type is stored without validation. The intake service then accepts votes as if the task were public, and the task never evaluates.

docs.title: 1.4 Task status
docs.text:
Status Set by Meaning "scheduled" the creator, in the create request Waiting for scheduled_time. The service does not set this for you. "started" VotingTaskInitiator Invitations sent, votes accepted "complete" VoteResultFinalizer Evaluation finished, report_json stored

A task created without "status": "scheduled" and a scheduled_time is stored but never picked up by the scheduler, so it never starts.

The services also write start_time (when the task starts) and end_time (when it completes) onto the task document. These fields are not part of the dataclass, so they appear in raw queries but not in parsed objects.

docs.title: 1.5 Current implementation gaps
docs.text:
These gaps were found by reading the code. Each one blocks or changes the flow in §1.2. Fix them, or work around them, before you rely on the system.

# Gap Effect 1 votes_submission/ and evaluator_job/ use an older schema.py. In that version, from_dict is Cls(**data), and the evaluation fields are strings named voting_pqt_dsl, choice_evaluation_dsl, tie_breaker_dsl, post_awarding_dsl, and voting_message_request_creator_dsl. MongoDB returns every document with an _id key. The old from_dict does not accept _id, so every read fails with TypeError, and POST /submit-vote returns 400 for every vote. Even after that is fixed, the documents that the submission service writes contain voting_pqt (a dict, §2.5), not voting_pqt_dsl. 2 VoteAcceptor checks the evaluation trigger before it saves the current vote. The vote that would complete the set is not counted. Public tasks evaluate on the vote after the threshold. Private tasks never evaluate, because the last listed voter's vote is never counted and nobody else can vote. 3 The Kubernetes Job is named after social_task_id, which has the form task_1a2b3c4d. Kubernetes object names cannot contain _, so the Job is rejected. The exception is caught by the PQT block, and the vote that triggered evaluation is stored as qualified = false. 4 VoteServers() and the evaluator's Initiator() and VoteResultFinalizer() are built with the default mongodb://localhost:27017. They ignore MONGO_URL. The evaluator Job is not given WORKFLOWS_API_URL. Vote intake and evaluation read a different database than the submission service unless MongoDB is on localhost. The evaluator calls http://localhost:5001 for workflows. 5 Invitations go to one Redis channel per voting option key, not per org_ids entry. Voters are not invited unless they are also options. This is the case in a peer election (§7). 6 scheduled_time is compared to a naive datetime.utcnow(). A scheduled_time with a UTC offset raises TypeError in the scheduler's refresh. One such task stops every task from being dispatched. A trailing Z is rejected at creation with 400 (Python 3.10 fromisoformat). 7 POST /generic-query/<collection> returns raw MongoDB documents. ObjectId is not JSON-serializable, so any query that matches at least one document returns 400. 8 If the invitation creator raises, or the subject spec is missing, the task status is not updated. The task stays "scheduled", and the scheduler retries it every 60 seconds, indefinitely. 9 job_id is never written. The field is always absent. Find the Job by name (social_task_id) in the votes-evaluation namespace.

docs.title: 2. Schema
docs.text:
All four entities are plain dataclasses (submission/core/schema.py). They round-trip through to_dict() / from_dict() and are stored as-is, with no ORM or mapping layer, as MongoDB documents. to_dict() writes datetimes as ISO-8601 strings. from_dict() accepts ISO-8601 strings (a trailing Z is allowed here), epoch seconds, or datetime objects.

A task is stored as three documents, one per entity, that share the same social_task_id. Votes are stored separately, one document per vote.

The create request uses different key names from the stored documents. The parser maps them, as shown in the "Request key" column below and in §3.2.

docs.title: 2.1 SocialTaskCoreData
docs.text:
The task itself: who created it, who may vote, when it starts, and its current state. Collection social_task_core_data.

Field Request key Type Required Description social_task_id — string auto Primary key, task_ plus 8 hex characters. Generated by the parser. A value in the request is ignored. created_by_subject_id created_by_subject_id string yes Who created the task. Used as sender_subject_id on invitations. created_by_subject_data created_by_subject_data object yes (may be {}) Free-form data about the creator. org_ids org_ids array<string> yes (may be []) Private: the fixed list of eligible voters. Evaluation waits for a qualified vote from every entry. Public: ignored. social_task_access_type access_type string yes "private" or "public". See §1.3. Not validated. goal_data goal object yes (may be {}) What the vote is meant to decide. Free-form. Passed to every hook. social_tasks_topics topics array<string> yes (may be []) Free-form topic labels. Stored only. No service filters on them. social_task_properties properties object yes (may be {}) Free-form properties such as urgency or category. creation_time creation_time datetime yes Supplied by the caller, not by the server. scheduled_time scheduled_time datetime | absent needed to start When the task should start. Naive ISO-8601, interpreted as UTC. See §1.5 gap 6. duration duration integer | absent no Public: the number of qualified votes that triggers evaluation (default 5). Not a time span. status status string | absent needed to start "scheduled", "started", or "complete". Must be "scheduled" at creation for the task to start. See §1.4. report_json report object auto ({}) Filled in by the evaluator job. See §2.6. job_id — string | absent unused Reserved. Never written. enable_live_streaming enable_live_streaming boolean no (default false) Whether the WebSocket live stream will serve this task. See §3.6.

to_dict() drops fields whose value is None, so unset optional fields are absent from the document, not null.

Example: SocialTaskCoreData document (private task, just created):

{
  "social_task_id": "task_3f9c6d2e",
  "created_by_subject_id": "planner-service",
  "created_by_subject_data": {"team": "localisation"},
  "org_ids": ["agent-reviewer-01", "agent-reviewer-02", "agent-reviewer-03"],
  "social_task_access_type": "private",
  "goal_data": {"objective": "Choose the lead translator for the Q4 handbook"},
  "social_tasks_topics": ["translation", "fr"],
  "social_task_properties": {"urgency": "high"},
  "creation_time": "2026-10-22T09:00:00",
  "scheduled_time": "2026-10-22T10:00:00",
  "status": "scheduled",
  "report_json": {},
  "enable_live_streaming": true
}

docs.title: 2.2 SocialChoiceSubjectSpecInput
docs.text:
What voters see: the topic and the options. Collection social_choice_subject_spec.

Field Request key Type Required Description social_task_id — string auto FK to SocialTaskCoreData.social_task_id. topic_title title string yes Short title shown to voters. topic_description description string yes What is being voted on. voting_options_map voting_options object yes Option ID → label. The keys double as addresses: one invitation channel per key (§5.2). voting_option_metadata_map voting_metadata object yes (may be {}) Option ID → extra data, for example a candidate's profile. supported_protocols supported_protocols array<string> yes (may be []) Stored only. Not read by any service. voting_message_request_creator voting_request function spec yes (may be {}) The invitation creator. {} disables it. See §2.5 and §4.2.

Example:

{
  "social_task_id": "task_3f9c6d2e",
  "topic_title": "Lead translator, Q4 handbook",
  "topic_description": "Pick the agent that will lead the EN→FR translation of the Q4 handbook.",
  "voting_options_map": {
    "agent-translator-01": "Translator 01",
    "agent-translator-02": "Translator 02",
    "agent-translator-03": "Translator 03"
  },
  "voting_option_metadata_map": {
    "agent-translator-01": {"languages": ["en", "fr"], "past_jobs": 42},
    "agent-translator-02": {"languages": ["en", "fr", "de"], "past_jobs": 17}
  },
  "supported_protocols": ["http"],
  "voting_message_request_creator": {
    "mode": "function",
    "function_id": "voting-invite-builder:1.0-stable",
    "parameters": {}
  }
}

docs.title: 2.3 SocialChoiceEvaluationInput
docs.text:
How votes are qualified and counted. Collection social_choice_evaluation_input.

Field Request key Type Required Description social_task_id — string auto FK to SocialTaskCoreData.social_task_id. constraints_entry_id constraints_primary string yes (may be "") Reserved. Stored, never read. constraints_entry_id_1 constraints_secondary string yes (may be "") Reserved. Stored, never read. voting_pqt voting_pqt function spec yes Pre-qualification test, run on every vote. See §4.3. choice_evaluation evaluation function spec yes Computes the winner or winners. See §4.4. tie_breaker tie_breaker function spec yes (may be {}) Runs only when choice evaluation returns more than one winner. See §4.5. post_awarding post_award function spec yes Runs after the winners are final. See §4.6.

Example:

{
  "social_task_id": "task_3f9c6d2e",
  "constraints_entry_id": "",
  "constraints_entry_id_1": "",
  "voting_pqt": {"mode": "dsl", "workflow_id": "vote-option-is-valid:1.0"},
  "choice_evaluation": {"mode": "dsl", "workflow_id": "plurality-count:1.0"},
  "tie_breaker": {"mode": "dsl", "workflow_id": "earliest-vote-wins:1.0"},
  "post_awarding": {"mode": "dsl", "workflow_id": "assign-lead-translator:1.0"}
}

The vote-intake service and the evaluator job currently read these hooks from string fields named voting_pqt_dsl, choice_evaluation_dsl, tie_breaker_dsl, and post_awarding_dsl. Those fields hold DSL workflow IDs. See §1.5 gap 1 and §4.1.

docs.title: 2.4 Votes
docs.text:
One subject's vote on one task. Collection votes.

Field Type Required Description vote_id string yes Primary key. Chosen by the client. The server does not generate it or check it for uniqueness. Use a UUID4. social_task_id string yes Which task this vote is for. submitter_subject_id string yes Who is voting. Must be in org_ids for private tasks. At most one vote per subject per task, counting disqualified votes. vote_data object yes The ballot itself. Free-form. Its shape is a contract between the creator and the PQT and evaluation hooks, for example {"selected_option": "agent-translator-02"} or a ranking. submission_time datetime must be present Overwritten with server time on receipt. The request must still include it (§3.4). qualified boolean must be present Overwritten with the PQT result. The request must still include it.

Example:

{
  "vote_id": "7d0f2a9c-2b4e-4a51-9a3e-0c6f1b2d4e8a",
  "social_task_id": "task_3f9c6d2e",
  "submitter_subject_id": "agent-reviewer-01",
  "vote_data": {"selected_option": "agent-translator-02"},
  "submission_time": "2026-10-22T10:03:12.481203",
  "qualified": true
}

docs.title: 2.5 Function spec
docs.text:
Each hook is configured with a small object that says where its logic lives. The same shape is used for voting_message_request_creator, voting_pqt, choice_evaluation, tie_breaker, and post_awarding.

Field Type Required Description mode string yes "function" (function registry) or "dsl" (DSL workflow registry). function_id string mode: "function" function_id in the function registry, for example voting-invite-builder:1.0-stable. parameters object no (default {}) mode: "function" only. Passed as per-call parameters when the function runs as a stateless job. workflow_id string mode: "dsl" Workflow ID in the DSL workflow registry. 
{"mode": "function", "function_id": "voting-invite-builder:1.0-stable", "parameters": {"tone": "formal"}}
{"mode": "dsl", "workflow_id": "plurality-count:1.0"}

An empty object {} disables the invitation creator and the tie-breaker. For the other hooks, {} is accepted at creation but fails when the hook runs.

docs.title: 2.6 report_json
docs.text:
Written to SocialTaskCoreData.report_json by the evaluator job when it finishes (§1.2 step 9).

Field Type Description task object SocialTaskCoreData.to_dict() at evaluation time subject_spec object SocialChoiceSubjectSpecInput.to_dict() evaluation_spec object SocialChoiceEvaluationInput.to_dict() votes array The qualified votes that were evaluated winners array<string> Final winners, after the tie-breaker if it ran post_award_payload object Output of the post-award hook dsl_outputs object Raw output of each hook that ran, keyed choice_evaluation_dsl, tie_breaker_dsl (only if it ran), and post_awarding_dsl evaluated_at string ISO-8601 UTC timestamp

Example:

{
  "task": {"social_task_id": "task_3f9c6d2e", "status": "started", "...": "..."},
  "subject_spec": {"topic_title": "Lead translator, Q4 handbook", "...": "..."},
  "evaluation_spec": {"...": "..."},
  "votes": [
    {"vote_id": "7d0f…", "submitter_subject_id": "agent-reviewer-01", "vote_data": {"selected_option": "agent-translator-02"}, "qualified": true, "...": "..."},
    {"vote_id": "c41a…", "submitter_subject_id": "agent-reviewer-02", "vote_data": {"selected_option": "agent-translator-02"}, "qualified": true, "...": "..."},
    {"vote_id": "e9b3…", "submitter_subject_id": "agent-reviewer-03", "vote_data": {"selected_option": "agent-translator-01"}, "qualified": true, "...": "..."}
  ],
  "winners": ["agent-translator-02"],
  "post_award_payload": {"assigned_to": "agent-translator-02", "start_by": "2026-10-23T09:00:00Z"},
  "dsl_outputs": {
    "choice_evaluation_dsl": {"winner": "agent-translator-02", "tally": {"agent-translator-02": 2, "agent-translator-01": 1}},
    "post_awarding_dsl": {"assigned_to": "agent-translator-02", "start_by": "2026-10-23T09:00:00Z"}
  },
  "evaluated_at": "2026-10-22T10:07:45.221000"
}

task.status in the report is "started", because the report is built before the status changes to "complete".

docs.title: 2.7 Storage
docs.text:
All entities live in MongoDB, database voting_db, one collection each.

Collection Keyed by Indexes social_task_core_data social_task_id none created by the services social_choice_subject_spec social_task_id none social_choice_evaluation_input social_task_id none votes vote_id none

get(), update(), and delete() work on the entity's own ID field, never on MongoDB's _id. update() is a $set on top-level fields. The scheduler reads the whole social_task_core_data collection on every poll, and the duplicate-vote check reads every vote for the task. Add indexes on social_task_id, status, and votes.social_task_id yourself if volumes grow.

docs.title: 3. APIs
docs.text:
The voting system exposes three HTTP servers and one WebSocket server. Routes are mounted at the root. There is no auth or ACL layer, so treat every endpoint as internal, trusted-network only.

Server Default address Endpoints Submission http://<host>:5000 §3.2, §3.3 Vote intake http://<host>:8081 §3.4 (plus NATS, §5.3) Query http://<host>:8082 §3.5 Live stream ws://<host>:8765 §3.6

docs.title: 3.1 Response format
docs.text:
There is no shared envelope. Success responses return the payload directly. Failures return:

{ "error": "human readable message" }

Each endpoint below lists its own success shape and status codes.

docs.title: 3.2 How to create a social task
docs.text:
POST /submit-social-choice-task (submission server)

Parses the request into the three entities in §2, generates a social_task_id, and inserts the three documents. No invitations are sent at this point. They go out when the scheduler starts the task (§1.2).

Request body. Three top-level objects. Every key listed is read with payload[...], so it must be present unless marked optional.

Path Maps to Notes social_task.created_by_subject_id created_by_subject_id social_task.created_by_subject_data created_by_subject_data object social_task.org_ids org_ids array of subject IDs social_task.access_type social_task_access_type "private" or "public" social_task.goal goal_data object social_task.topics social_tasks_topics array social_task.properties social_task_properties object social_task.creation_time creation_time ISO-8601, no Z social_task.scheduled_time scheduled_time optional. Naive ISO-8601 in UTC. Needed to start. social_task.duration duration optional. Public vote threshold. social_task.status status optional. Send "scheduled" for the task to start. social_task.report report_json optional, default {} social_task.enable_live_streaming enable_live_streaming optional, default false subject_spec.title topic_title subject_spec.description topic_description subject_spec.voting_options voting_options_map object, option ID → label subject_spec.voting_metadata voting_option_metadata_map object subject_spec.supported_protocols supported_protocols array subject_spec.voting_request voting_message_request_creator function spec, or {} evaluation_spec.constraints_primary constraints_entry_id string, may be "" evaluation_spec.constraints_secondary constraints_entry_id_1 string, may be "" evaluation_spec.voting_pqt voting_pqt function spec evaluation_spec.evaluation choice_evaluation function spec evaluation_spec.tie_breaker tie_breaker function spec, or {} evaluation_spec.post_award post_awarding function spec

Function specs are described in §2.5.

Private-task example. Three named reviewers choose between three translators. The task starts at 10:00 UTC.

curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/submit-social-choice-task \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "social_task": {
      "created_by_subject_id": "planner-service",
      "created_by_subject_data": {"team": "localisation"},
      "org_ids": ["agent-reviewer-01", "agent-reviewer-02", "agent-reviewer-03"],
      "access_type": "private",
      "goal": {"objective": "Choose the lead translator for the Q4 handbook"},
      "topics": ["translation", "fr"],
      "properties": {"urgency": "high"},
      "creation_time": "2026-10-22T09:00:00",
      "scheduled_time": "2026-10-22T10:00:00",
      "status": "scheduled",
      "enable_live_streaming": true
    },
    "subject_spec": {
      "title": "Lead translator, Q4 handbook",
      "description": "Pick the agent that will lead the EN→FR translation of the Q4 handbook.",
      "voting_options": {
        "agent-translator-01": "Translator 01",
        "agent-translator-02": "Translator 02",
        "agent-translator-03": "Translator 03"
      },
      "voting_metadata": {},
      "supported_protocols": ["http"],
      "voting_request": {"mode": "function", "function_id": "voting-invite-builder:1.0-stable"}
    },
    "evaluation_spec": {
      "constraints_primary": "",
      "constraints_secondary": "",
      "voting_pqt": {"mode": "dsl", "workflow_id": "vote-option-is-valid:1.0"},
      "evaluation": {"mode": "dsl", "workflow_id": "plurality-count:1.0"},
      "tie_breaker": {"mode": "dsl", "workflow_id": "earliest-vote-wins:1.0"},
      "post_award": {"mode": "dsl", "workflow_id": "assign-lead-translator:1.0"}
    }
  }'

Public-task example. Changes from the private example: access_type is "public", org_ids is empty, and evaluation fires at 10 qualified votes.

{
  "social_task": {
    "access_type": "public",
    "org_ids": [],
    "duration": 10,
    "...": "same as above"
  },
  "subject_spec": { "...": "same as above" },
  "evaluation_spec": { "...": "same as above" }
}

Response 201 Created:

{ "social_task_id": "task_3f9c6d2e" }

Error responses:

Status When 400 Empty or non-JSON body; one of social_task, subject_spec, evaluation_spec is missing; creation_time or scheduled_time is not a valid ISO-8601 string (a trailing Z is rejected) 500 A nested key is missing (KeyError), or the database insert fails. The body is always {"error": "Internal server error"}. Check the service log for the missing key.

Creation does not validate access_type, function specs, or whether status and scheduled_time are set. A task can be created successfully and still never start. See §1.4.

docs.title: 3.3 How to validate a task without creating it
docs.text:
POST /parse-social-choice-task (submission server)

Runs the same parser as §3.2 and returns the result without writing anything. Use it to check a payload and see the stored field names.

curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/parse-social-choice-task \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @task.json

Response 200:

{
  "parsed": {
    "social_task": { "...": "SocialTaskCoreData.to_dict()" },
    "subject_spec": { "...": "SocialChoiceSubjectSpecInput.to_dict()" },
    "evaluation_spec": { "...": "SocialChoiceEvaluationInput.to_dict()" }
  }
}

The social_task_id in the response is freshly generated and is not reserved. §3.2 generates a different ID. Errors are the same as §3.2.

docs.title: 3.4 How to submit a vote
docs.text:
POST /submit-vote (vote-intake server, port 8081)

curl -X POST http://localhost:8081/submit-vote \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "vote_id": "7d0f2a9c-2b4e-4a51-9a3e-0c6f1b2d4e8a",
    "social_task_id": "task_3f9c6d2e",
    "submitter_subject_id": "agent-reviewer-01",
    "vote_data": {"selected_option": "agent-translator-02"},
    "submission_time": "2026-10-22T10:03:12",
    "qualified": false
  }'

The body must contain exactly the six Votes fields, no more and no fewer, because it is parsed with Votes(**data). The server overwrites submission_time and qualified, so any placeholder values work. The client chooses vote_id.

Processing order inside VoteAcceptor.accept_vote:

  1. Reject if submitter_subject_id already has a vote on this task, qualified or not.
  2. Reject if the task does not exist.
  3. Reject if the task status is not "started".
  4. Private only: reject if submitter_subject_id is not in org_ids.
  5. Load the subject spec and evaluation spec. Reject if either is missing, or if no PQT is configured.
  6. Run the PQT with the task, both specs, and vote_data (§4.3). qualified is bool(result["qualified"]).
  7. Check whether evaluation should start, and if so, launch the Kubernetes Job (§1.2 step 7).
  8. If step 6 or step 7 raised, set qualified = false.
  9. Persist the vote with the server's submission_time and the computed qualified.

Response 200:

{ "status": "accepted", "qualified": true }

"status": "accepted" means the vote was stored. A disqualified vote also returns 200, with "qualified": false, and still counts as this subject's one vote.

Error responses:

Status When 400 Any failure: a missing or extra field, a rejection in steps 1 to 5, or a database error. The message is in error, for example "Vote rejected: Vote already submitted for this task."

Rejection messages from steps 1 to 5:

Message Step Vote rejected: Vote already submitted for this task. 1 Vote rejected: Invalid social_task_id. 2 Vote rejected: Voting task is not active yet. 3 (also returned after the task is complete) Vote rejected: You are not authorized to vote in this private task. 4 Voting task configuration is incomplete. 5 Voting PQT DSL is not defined. 5

The winner is not returned from this call. Poll GET /get-status/<id> until it returns "complete", then read GET /get-report/<id> (§3.5). You can also subscribe to the winner's NATS subject (§5.4).

docs.title: 3.5 Query endpoints
docs.text:
All on the query server (port 8082).

Method Path Purpose GET /get-status/<social_task_id> Current task status GET /get-report/<social_task_id> The final report_json GET /get-full-task-bundle/<social_task_id> Task, specs, and all votes GET /is-live-streaming-enabled/<social_task_id> Whether §3.6 will serve this task POST /generic-query/<collection_name> Raw MongoDB filter on one collection

Every endpoint returns 400 {"error": "..."} on any failure, including an unknown social_task_id (for example "Error fetching status: Task not found."). None of them return 404.

docs.title: GET /get-status/<social_task_id>
docs.text:
curl http://localhost:8082/get-status/task_3f9c6d2e

→ 200 { "status": "started" }. The value is null if the task was created without a status.

docs.title: GET /get-report/<social_task_id>
docs.text:
curl http://localhost:8082/get-report/task_3f9c6d2e

→ 200 with the report_json object itself, unwrapped (§2.6). Before the task completes, this is {}.

docs.title: GET /get-full-task-bundle/<social_task_id>
docs.text:
curl http://localhost:8082/get-full-task-bundle/task_3f9c6d2e

→ 200:

{
  "task": { "...": "SocialTaskCoreData.to_dict()" },
  "subject_spec": { "...": "SocialChoiceSubjectSpecInput.to_dict()" },
  "evaluation_input": { "...": "SocialChoiceEvaluationInput.to_dict()" },
  "votes": [ { "...": "Votes.to_dict()" } ]
}

votes includes disqualified votes. Filter on qualified yourself. Note the key is evaluation_input, not evaluation_spec as in the report.

docs.title: GET /is-live-streaming-enabled/<social_task_id>
docs.text: → 200 { "enabled": true }

docs.title: POST /generic-query/<collection_name>
docs.text:
The body is a raw MongoDB filter document passed to collection.find(). collection_name must be one of social_task_core_data, social_choice_subject_spec, social_choice_evaluation_input, or votes. Any other name returns 400 {"error": "Error during query: Unsupported collection: ..."}.

# every task that is currently accepting votes
curl -X POST http://localhost:8082/generic-query/social_task_core_data \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"status": "started"}'

# every vote a subject has cast
curl -X POST http://localhost:8082/generic-query/votes \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"submitter_subject_id": "agent-reviewer-01"}'

This endpoint returns documents with MongoDB's _id, which is not JSON-serializable. Today, any query that matches at least one document returns 400, and only an empty result succeeds (200 []). See §1.5 gap 7. Until that is fixed, use the per-task endpoints above.

docs.title: 3.6 WebSocket live stream
docs.text:
ws://<host>:8765 (query system). The path is not checked.

The server pushes the full task bundle on a fixed interval, so dashboards can watch votes arrive. It serves only tasks created with enable_live_streaming: true.

1. Connect and send one JSON message:

{ "social_task_id": "task_3f9c6d2e", "refresh_interval": 5 }
Field Type Default Notes social_task_id string required refresh_interval int 5 Seconds between pushes

2. The server checks the task, then streams:

{
  "type": "update",
  "data": {
    "task": { "...": "..." },
    "subject_spec": { "...": "..." },
    "evaluation_input": { "...": "..." },
    "votes": [ "..." ]
  }
}

data is the same object as GET /get-full-task-bundle (§3.5). One message is sent every refresh_interval seconds until the client disconnects. The stream does not stop when the task completes. Watch data.task.status and disconnect yourself.

Errors. The server sends one message and closes:

Message When {"error": "Missing social_task_id"} The field is absent {"error": "Invalid request format. Must be JSON with 'social_task_id' and 'refresh_interval'"} The first message is not JSON, or refresh_interval is not an integer {"error": "Live streaming not enabled for this task"} enable_live_streaming is false

An unknown social_task_id closes the connection without an error message. If a single push fails, for example on a database error, the failure is logged and the next push is attempted on schedule.

Example client:

import asyncio, json
import websockets

async def watch(task_id: str):
    async with websockets.connect("ws://localhost:8765") as ws:
        await ws.send(json.dumps({"social_task_id": task_id, "refresh_interval": 5}))
        async for raw in ws:
            msg = json.loads(raw)
            if "error" in msg:
                raise RuntimeError(msg["error"])
            task = msg["data"]["task"]
            votes = msg["data"]["votes"]
            print(task.get("status"), len(votes), "votes")
            if task.get("status") == "complete":
                break

asyncio.run(watch("task_3f9c6d2e"))

docs.text: ← Back to index

docs.title: 4. Functions to write (invitation, PQT, evaluation, tie-breaker, post-award)
docs.text:
The voting system does not count votes itself. Every decision is delegated to one of five hooks configured on the task:

Hook Field Runs in When Required Invitation creator voting_message_request_creator Submission service Once, when the task starts no PQT voting_pqt Vote-intake service Once per vote, inline yes Choice evaluation choice_evaluation Evaluator job Once per task yes Tie-breaker tie_breaker Evaluator job Only if choice evaluation returns more than one winner no Post-award post_awarding Evaluator job Once per task, after the winners are final yes

Every hook receives a single JSON object as input and must return a single JSON object as output. The services read only the keys documented below. A malformed response either disqualifies the vote (PQT) or makes the evaluator job exit with an error and no report (the other evaluation hooks). Nothing is retried.

docs.title: 4.1 Two ways to plug in logic
docs.text:
A hook's function spec picks where its logic lives:

  • mode: "function": a function in the function registry (FUNCTIONS_REGISTRY_URL), referenced by function_id. It runs through AgentFunctions (submission/core/evaluators/agents_functions/), which supports the same three execution modes as the bidding system:
  • external (is_external=True): a plain HTTP POST of the input JSON to external_function_url. The response's "data" key is returned, or the whole body if there is no "data" key.
  • stateful (is_stateful=True): deployed as a long-lived service on first use. The deployment is named <function_name>-<SOCIAL_CHOICE_ID>.
  • stateless: run once per call as a registry-managed job on EXECUTOR_ID, with the spec's parameters.

The hook's output is read from the job_output_data key of the call result. - mode: "dsl": a workflow in the DSL workflow registry, referenced by workflow_id. The workflow's final output is the hook's output.

Which hooks support which mode today. Only the invitation creator goes through the mode switch (execute_functionality in submission/core/evaluators/__init__.py). The PQT, choice evaluation, tie-breaker, and post-award hooks are run by dsl_executor's new_dsl_workflow_executor against WORKFLOWS_API_URL, from the string fields voting_pqt_dsl, choice_evaluation_dsl, tie_breaker_dsl, and post_awarding_dsl. In practice those four hooks are DSL workflows only until the vote-intake and evaluator services move to the new schema (§1.5 gap 1).

docs.title: Authoring format: AIOSv1PolicyRule
docs.text:
Stateful and stateless registry functions, and the policy nodes inside a DSL workflow, are all written the same way: as a class named exactly AIOSv1PolicyRule. The runtime instantiates it from your code and calls eval().

import logging


class AIOSv1PolicyRule:

    def __init__(self, rule_id, settings, parameters):
        """
        Args:
            rule_id (str): Unique identifier for the rule.
            settings (dict): Configuration settings for the rule.
            parameters (dict): Parameters defining the rule's behavior.
        """
        self.rule_id = rule_id
        self.settings = settings
        self.parameters = parameters

    def eval(self, parameters, input_data, context):
        logging.info("input: {}".format(input_data))
        # ... decide, return a dict
Piece What it holds here settings / parameters (constructor) Static configuration stored with the function: thresholds, weights, allowed options. Read your tunables from these. Treat __init__ as one-time setup, because a stateful deployment reuses the instance. input_data (eval) The input contract of the hook, as described below. Every hook's input is wrapped in a user_input key. parameters (eval) The function spec's parameters, for a stateless registry function. Empty otherwise. context (eval) Owned by the execution runtime. Nothing in the voting services depends on it. return value A JSON-serializable dict: the output contract of the hook.

For an external function (is_external=True), the class contract does not apply. Any HTTP service that accepts the input JSON and returns the output JSON works.

docs.title: Common input
docs.text:
All hooks receive the task's configuration as dicts, wrapped in user_input:

Key Content Hooks user_input.task SocialTaskCoreData.to_dict() all user_input.subject_spec SocialChoiceSubjectSpecInput.to_dict() all user_input.evaluation_spec SocialChoiceEvaluationInput.to_dict() all except the invitation creator

Each hook adds its own keys, as listed in its section.

docs.title: 4.2 Invitation creator
docs.text:
Purpose: build custom content for the invitation that goes out when the task starts. For example: a personalised prompt, a deadline, or a ballot schema.

When it's called: once, by VotingTaskInitiator, just before the invitations are published. It is skipped if voting_message_request_creator is {}.

Input contract:

{
  "user_input": {
    "task": { "...": "SocialTaskCoreData.to_dict()" },
    "subject_spec": { "...": "SocialChoiceSubjectSpecInput.to_dict()" }
  }
}

Output contract: any JSON object. It is placed verbatim in the invitation's event_data.custom_data (§5.2). The same content goes to every recipient, because the hook runs once per task, not once per recipient.

If the hook raises, no invitations are sent, the task stays "scheduled", and the scheduler retries it every 60 seconds (§1.5 gap 8).

Reference implementation (AIOSv1PolicyRule, stateless or stateful registry function):

import logging


class AIOSv1PolicyRule:

    def __init__(self, rule_id, settings, parameters):
        self.rule_id = rule_id
        self.settings = settings
        self.parameters = parameters

    def eval(self, parameters, input_data, context):
        logging.info("invite input: {}".format(input_data))

        spec = input_data["user_input"]["subject_spec"]
        return {
            "prompt": f"Please vote: {spec['topic_title']}",
            "ballot_schema": {"selected_option": list(spec["voting_options_map"].keys())},
            "vote_endpoint": self.settings.get("vote_endpoint", "http://voting-intake:8081/submit-vote"),
        }

Alternative reference implementation (external HTTP mode, Flask):

from flask import Flask, request, jsonify

app = Flask(__name__)

@app.post("/")
def build_invite():
    spec = request.get_json()["user_input"]["subject_spec"]
    return jsonify({"data": {"job_output_data": {
        "prompt": f"Please vote: {spec['topic_title']}",
        "ballot_schema": {"selected_option": list(spec["voting_options_map"].keys())},
    }}})

The extra job_output_data level is needed because the submission service reads the hook's output from that key (§4.1).

docs.title: 4.3 PQT (pre-qualification test)
docs.text:
Purpose: decide whether a single vote counts. For example: reject a ballot that names an option that doesn't exist, a malformed ranking, or a voter who fails an external eligibility check.

When it's called: inline, synchronously, inside POST /submit-vote (or the NATS vote.submit handler), once per vote, after the initial checks in §3.4 pass. The PQT is mandatory. A task without one rejects every vote.

Input contract:

{
  "user_input": {
    "task": { "...": "..." },
    "subject_spec": { "...": "..." },
    "evaluation_spec": { "...": "..." },
    "vote_data": { "...": "the vote's vote_data only" }
  }
}

The DSL executor is also given addons: {"submitter_subject_id": "<voter>"}. vote_data does not carry the voter's ID, so read it from the addons if your rule needs it.

Output contract:

Key Type Required Meaning qualified boolean yes Truthy: the vote is stored with qualified = true and counts toward evaluation. Falsy or missing: the vote is stored with qualified = false. It is ignored by evaluation, but it still uses up the voter's one vote. (anything else) any no Ignored. A reason field is useful for your own logs, but it is not returned to the voter.

Unlike the bidding PQT, a negative verdict does not reject the request. The voter gets 200 with "qualified": false.

Example output:

{ "qualified": false, "reason": "option 'agent-translator-09' is not on the ballot" }

Reference implementation (AIOSv1PolicyRule policy node, option must be on the ballot):

import logging


class AIOSv1PolicyRule:

    def __init__(self, rule_id, settings, parameters):
        self.rule_id = rule_id
        self.settings = settings
        self.parameters = parameters

    def eval(self, parameters, input_data, context):
        logging.info("pqt input: {}".format(input_data))

        ui = input_data["user_input"]
        options = ui["subject_spec"]["voting_options_map"]
        choice = ui["vote_data"].get("selected_option")

        if choice not in options:
            return {"qualified": False, "reason": f"option {choice!r} is not on the ballot"}
        return {"qualified": True}

docs.title: 4.4 Choice evaluation
docs.text:
Purpose: given every qualified vote, decide the winner or winners. This is where the social-choice rule lives: plurality, Borda, approval, Condorcet, weighted voting, and so on.

When it's called: once per task, inside the evaluator job, after the trigger condition in §1.3 is met.

Input contract:

{
  "user_input": {
    "task": { "...": "..." },
    "subject_spec": { "...": "..." },
    "evaluation_spec": { "...": "..." },
    "votes": [ { "...": "Votes.to_dict()" }, "... qualified votes only" ]
  }
}

The DSL executor is also given addons: {"social_task_id": "<id>"}.

Output contract:

Key Type Required Meaning winner string one of winner / winners A single winner. Checked first. winners array<string> one of winner / winners One or more winners. More than one triggers the tie-breaker, if configured. (anything else) any no Kept in report_json.dsl_outputs.choice_evaluation_dsl. A good place for the tally.

If neither key is present, the job raises and exits with no report, and the task stays "started".

Winners should be option keys. The result notification is published on a NATS subject named after each winner (§5.4), so when the options are subject IDs, the winning subjects are notified directly.

Example output:

{
  "winner": "agent-translator-02",
  "tally": {"agent-translator-02": 2, "agent-translator-01": 1}
}

Reference implementation (plurality: most selected_option votes wins, and every option tied for first is returned):

import logging
from collections import Counter


class AIOSv1PolicyRule:

    def __init__(self, rule_id, settings, parameters):
        self.rule_id = rule_id
        self.settings = settings
        self.parameters = parameters

    def eval(self, parameters, input_data, context):
        logging.info("evaluation input: {}".format(input_data))

        votes = input_data["user_input"]["votes"]
        tally = Counter(v["vote_data"]["selected_option"] for v in votes)
        if not tally:
            return {"winners": [], "tally": {}}

        top = max(tally.values())
        winners = sorted(opt for opt, n in tally.items() if n == top)
        return {"winners": winners, "tally": dict(tally)}

An empty winners list passes through to post-award and the report, and no one is notified. Decide whether your post-award hook should treat it as "no decision".

Ranked-ballot variant (Borda count, with vote_data of the form {"ranking": ["agent-translator-02", "agent-translator-01", ...]}):

def eval(self, parameters, input_data, context):
    ui = input_data["user_input"]
    options = list(ui["subject_spec"]["voting_options_map"].keys())
    n = len(options)
    scores = {opt: 0 for opt in options}

    for v in ui["votes"]:
        for position, opt in enumerate(v["vote_data"]["ranking"]):
            if opt in scores:
                scores[opt] += n - 1 - position

    top = max(scores.values())
    return {"winners": [o for o, s in scores.items() if s == top], "scores": scores}

docs.title: 4.5 Tie-breaker
docs.text:
Purpose: reduce several tied winners to fewer, usually one.

When it's called: inside the evaluator job, only if choice evaluation returned more than one winner and a tie-breaker is configured. If no tie-breaker is configured, all tied winners are final.

Input contract: the choice-evaluation input, plus the tied winners:

{
  "user_input": {
    "task": { "...": "..." },
    "subject_spec": { "...": "..." },
    "evaluation_spec": { "...": "..." },
    "votes": [ "..." ],
    "winners": ["agent-translator-01", "agent-translator-02"]
  }
}

Output contract: the same as choice evaluation. Return winner or winners. The result replaces the winner list and is not checked again, so returning more than one winner leaves the tie in place.

Reference implementation (earliest vote for any tied option wins):

def eval(self, parameters, input_data, context):
    ui = input_data["user_input"]
    tied = set(ui["winners"])
    ballots = sorted(
        (v for v in ui["votes"] if v["vote_data"].get("selected_option") in tied),
        key=lambda v: v["submission_time"],
    )
    return {"winner": ballots[0]["vote_data"]["selected_option"], "rule": "earliest_vote"}

docs.title: 4.6 Post-award
docs.text:
Purpose: turn the decision into action and describe it for the winners. For example: assign work, record an agreement, or set a start time.

When it's called: once per task, inside the evaluator job, after the winners are final. It always runs, even when the winner list is empty.

Input contract: the choice-evaluation input, plus the final winners:

{
  "user_input": {
    "task": { "...": "..." },
    "subject_spec": { "...": "..." },
    "evaluation_spec": { "...": "..." },
    "votes": [ "..." ],
    "winners": ["agent-translator-02"]
  }
}

Output contract: any JSON object. It becomes post_award_payload, which is stored in report_json and sent to every winner in the voting_result notification (§5.4). Put everything the winners need to act on here.

Example output:

{
  "assigned_to": "agent-translator-02",
  "start_by": "2026-10-23T09:00:00Z",
  "document_url": "https://storage.example.com/docs/q4-handbook.pdf"
}

Reference implementation:

def eval(self, parameters, input_data, context):
    ui = input_data["user_input"]
    winners = ui["winners"]
    if not winners:
        return {"decision": "none", "reason": "no qualified votes"}
    return {
        "decision": "assigned",
        "assigned_to": winners[0],
        "goal": ui["task"].get("goal_data", {}),
    }

docs.title: 4.7 Registering hooks
docs.text:
Every function_id and workflow_id must exist in its registry before the hook runs. Nothing is checked at task creation, so a missing hook fails late:

Hook Failure when the ID is not registered Invitation creator AgentFunctions.add() raises ValueError. The task stays "scheduled" and is retried every minute. PQT The workflow call raises, and every vote is stored with qualified = false. Choice evaluation, tie-breaker, post-award The evaluator job exits with an error. There is no report, and the task stays "started".

Registering a function (its function_type, is_external, external_function_url, and so on) or a DSL workflow is done against the registry service directly, outside the voting system's API.

Use POST /parse-social-choice-task to confirm the stored field names. Then run each hook against its registry with a sample user_input before you create a real task.

docs.text: ← Back to index

docs.title: 5. Messaging: how subjects hear about votes
docs.text:
Where the bidding system routes every message through a delegate service, the voting system publishes directly to two message buses:

Message Direction Transport Address voting_invite system → subjects Redis pub/sub (ORG_REDIS_URL) one channel per voting option key vote submission subjects → system NATS (ORG_NATS_URL) subject vote.submit voting_result system → subjects NATS (ORG_NATS_URL) one subject per winner

Votes can also be submitted over REST (§3.4), and progress can be watched over the WebSocket live stream (§3.6).

docs.title: 5.1 Delivery guarantees
docs.text:
None. Redis pub/sub and core NATS both drop a message if no one is subscribed when it is published. The system does not record what was sent, retry, or wait for acknowledgements. Compare the bidding system's BidTaskResult.

As a result:

  • Subscribe before a task's scheduled_time to be sure you get the invitation.
  • Treat invitations and results as hints. The source of truth is the query API: GET /get-status/<id> and GET /get-report/<id> (§3.5).

docs.title: 5.2 voting_invite: sent when a task starts
docs.text:
Published by VotingTaskInitiator when the scheduler starts a task (§1.2 step 4), before the status changes to "started".

Transport: Redis PUBLISH on ORG_REDIS_URL (default redis://localhost:6379/0). The same payload is published once on a channel named after each key of voting_options_map.

{
  "event_type": "voting_invite",
  "sender_subject_id": "planner-service",
  "event_data": {
    "custom_data": { "...": "invitation creator output, or {}" },
    "voting_info": {
      "social_task_id": "task_3f9c6d2e",
      "topic_title": "Lead translator, Q4 handbook",
      "topic_description": "Pick the agent that will lead the EN→FR translation of the Q4 handbook.",
      "voting_options_map": { "agent-translator-01": "Translator 01", "...": "..." },
      "voting_option_metadata_map": { "...": "..." },
      "supported_protocols": ["http"],
      "voting_message_request_creator": { "...": "..." }
    }
  }
}
Field Value event_type always "voting_invite" sender_subject_id the task's created_by_subject_id event_data.custom_data output of the invitation creator (§4.2), or {} event_data.voting_info the full subject spec. Read social_task_id from here to vote.

The invitation does not include org_ids, the access type, or the goal. If a recipient needs them, it fetches GET /get-full-task-bundle/<id>.

Who is invited. Invitations go to the option keys, not to org_ids. If your options are candidate subjects and the voters are a different set of subjects, the voters are not invited. Tell them about the task another way. Invitations reach voters only when every voter is also an option, as in a peer election (§7). See §1.5 gap 5.

Subscribing:

import json
import redis

r = redis.Redis.from_url("redis://org-redis:6379/0", decode_responses=True)
pubsub = r.pubsub()
pubsub.subscribe("agent-translator-01")      # your subject ID

for msg in pubsub.listen():
    if msg["type"] != "message":
        continue
    event = json.loads(msg["data"])
    if event.get("event_type") == "voting_invite":
        task_id = event["event_data"]["voting_info"]["social_task_id"]
        print("invited to", task_id)

docs.title: 5.3 Vote submission over NATS
docs.text:
The vote-intake service subscribes to the NATS subject vote.submit on ORG_NATS_URL (default nats://localhost:4222). A message there is handled exactly like POST /submit-vote (§3.4), and its body has the same six-field shape.

import asyncio, json, uuid
from nats.aio.client import Client as NATS

async def vote():
    nc = NATS()
    await nc.connect(servers=["nats://org-nats:4222"])
    await nc.publish("vote.submit", json.dumps({
        "vote_id": str(uuid.uuid4()),
        "social_task_id": "task_3f9c6d2e",
        "submitter_subject_id": "agent-reviewer-01",
        "vote_data": {"selected_option": "agent-translator-02"},
        "submission_time": "2026-10-22T10:03:12",
        "qualified": False,
    }).encode())
    await nc.drain()

asyncio.run(vote())

There is no reply. A rejected or disqualified vote is only logged by the service. To learn the outcome, query the vote afterwards (GET /get-full-task-bundle/<id>), or use REST, which returns qualified and any rejection message.

docs.title: 5.4 voting_result: sent after evaluation
docs.text:
Published by the evaluator job's ResultNotifier after the report is stored (§1.2 step 10).

Transport: NATS PUBLISH on ORG_NATS_URL. The same payload is published once on a subject named after each winner. Losers, voters, and the creator are not notified.

{
  "event_type": "voting_result",
  "task_id": "task_3f9c6d2e",
  "event_data": {
    "social_task_id": "task_3f9c6d2e",
    "winners": ["agent-translator-02"],
    "post_award_payload": { "...": "post-award hook output verbatim" }
  }
}

The payload is deliberately lean, like the bidding system's bid_winner. Everything the winner needs to act on must be put into post_award_payload by the post-award hook (§4.6). The full context is in GET /get-report/<id>.

Anyone else who needs the outcome, such as the creator, the voters, or a dashboard, polls GET /get-status/<id> until it returns "complete", or watches the live stream (§3.6).

Subscribing:

import asyncio, json
from nats.aio.client import Client as NATS

async def listen(subject_id: str):
    nc = NATS()
    await nc.connect(servers=["nats://org-nats:4222"])

    async def on_msg(msg):
        event = json.loads(msg.data.decode())
        if event.get("event_type") == "voting_result":
            print("won", event["task_id"], event["event_data"]["post_award_payload"])

    await nc.subscribe(subject_id, cb=on_msg)
    while True:
        await asyncio.sleep(1)

asyncio.run(listen("agent-translator-02"))

docs.title: 5.5 Sharing a bus with other traffic
docs.text:
Both buses address subjects by their bare subject ID: the Redis channel agent-translator-01 and the NATS subject agent-translator-01. Other systems on the same Redis or NATS may use the same names. Always check event_type before you act on a message, and ignore types you don't recognise.

docs.title: 6. Using the system from Python
docs.text: The voting system does not ship a client library yet. Compare the bidding system's bidding_client.py. This page provides a minimal, single-file client that you can copy into your project. It wraps the REST APIs in §3 and covers the invitation subscription from §5.2. Its only dependencies are requests and, for the subscription, redis.

docs.title: 6.1 Quick reference
docs.text: Method Server Returns Purpose VotingClient.create_task(payload) submission str (task ID) Create a social task (§3.2) VotingClient.parse_task(payload) submission dict Validate a payload without storing it (§3.3) VotingClient.submit_vote(task_id, subject_id, vote_data) vote intake bool (qualified) Cast a vote (§3.4) VotingClient.get_status(task_id) query str \| None Current status VotingClient.get_report(task_id) query dict Final report ({} until complete) VotingClient.get_bundle(task_id) query dict Task, specs, and all votes VotingClient.wait_for_result(task_id, ...) query dict Poll until "complete", then return the report InviteListener Redis thread Calls listener.on_voting_invite(event) for each invitation

docs.title: 6.2 The client
docs.text:
Save as voting_client.py:

# voting_client.py
import json
import logging
import threading
import time
import uuid
from typing import Any, Dict, Optional

import requests

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class VotingError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, status_code: Optional[int], message: str):
        super().__init__(f"[{status_code}] {message}" if status_code else message)
        self.status_code = status_code
        self.message = message


class VotingClient:
    """Thin wrapper over the three voting HTTP servers. Not thread-safe:
    use one instance per thread."""

    def __init__(self, submission_url: str, intake_url: str, query_url: str,
                 timeout=(5, 30), session: Optional[requests.Session] = None):
        self.submission_url = submission_url.rstrip("/")
        self.intake_url = intake_url.rstrip("/")
        self.query_url = query_url.rstrip("/")
        self.timeout = timeout
        self.session = session or requests.Session()

    # ---- transport ----

    def _request(self, method: str, url: str, **kwargs) -> Any:
        try:
            resp = self.session.request(method, url, timeout=self.timeout, **kwargs)
        except requests.RequestException as e:
            raise VotingError(None, str(e)) from e
        try:
            body = resp.json()
        except ValueError:
            body = {"error": resp.text}
        if resp.status_code >= 400:
            msg = body.get("error", resp.text) if isinstance(body, dict) else resp.text
            raise VotingError(resp.status_code, msg)
        return body

    # ---- tasks ----

    def create_task(self, payload: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
        body = self._request("POST", f"{self.submission_url}/submit-social-choice-task", json=payload)
        return body["social_task_id"]

    def parse_task(self, payload: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return self._request("POST", f"{self.submission_url}/parse-social-choice-task", json=payload)["parsed"]

    # ---- votes ----

    def submit_vote(self, social_task_id: str, submitter_subject_id: str,
                    vote_data: Dict[str, Any], vote_id: Optional[str] = None) -> bool:
        body = self._request("POST", f"{self.intake_url}/submit-vote", json={
            "vote_id": vote_id or str(uuid.uuid4()),
            "social_task_id": social_task_id,
            "submitter_subject_id": submitter_subject_id,
            "vote_data": vote_data,
            # required by the server's parser, then overwritten
            "submission_time": "1970-01-01T00:00:00",
            "qualified": False,
        })
        return bool(body["qualified"])

    # ---- queries ----

    def get_status(self, social_task_id: str) -> Optional[str]:
        return self._request("GET", f"{self.query_url}/get-status/{social_task_id}")["status"]

    def get_report(self, social_task_id: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return self._request("GET", f"{self.query_url}/get-report/{social_task_id}")

    def get_bundle(self, social_task_id: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return self._request("GET", f"{self.query_url}/get-full-task-bundle/{social_task_id}")

    def wait_for_result(self, social_task_id: str, *, interval_seconds: float = 10,
                        timeout_seconds: Optional[float] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout_seconds if timeout_seconds else None
        while self.get_status(social_task_id) != "complete":
            if deadline and time.monotonic() > deadline:
                raise TimeoutError(f"task {social_task_id} not complete after {timeout_seconds}s")
            time.sleep(interval_seconds)
        return self.get_report(social_task_id)


class InviteListener(threading.Thread):
    """Subscribes to a subject's Redis channel and calls
    listener.on_voting_invite(event) for every voting_invite."""

    def __init__(self, redis_url: str, subject_id: str, listener):
        super().__init__(daemon=True, name=f"voting-invites-{subject_id}")
        import redis  # only needed for invitations
        self._redis = redis.Redis.from_url(redis_url, decode_responses=True)
        self._pubsub = self._redis.pubsub()
        self._pubsub.subscribe(subject_id)
        self._listener = listener
        self._stop = threading.Event()

    def run(self):
        while not self._stop.is_set():
            msg = self._pubsub.get_message(timeout=1.0)
            if not msg or msg["type"] != "message":
                continue
            try:
                event = json.loads(msg["data"])
            except ValueError:
                continue
            if event.get("event_type") != "voting_invite":
                continue
            try:
                self._listener.on_voting_invite(event)
            except Exception:
                log.exception("on_voting_invite failed")

    def stop(self, timeout: Optional[float] = None):
        self._stop.set()
        if threading.current_thread() is not self:
            self.join(timeout)
        self._pubsub.close()

Construct it with all three base URLs. The client never reads environment variables, so your code decides where the URLs come from:

from voting_client import VotingClient, VotingError, InviteListener

client = VotingClient(
    submission_url="http://voting-submission:5000",
    intake_url="http://voting-intake:8081",
    query_url="http://voting-query:8082",
)

InviteListener subscribes in its constructor, so it receives invitations published from that moment on, even before start() is called. Messages are then delivered once the thread starts.

docs.title: 6.4 Casting a vote
docs.text:
try:
    qualified = client.submit_vote(task_id, "agent-reviewer-01",
                                   {"selected_option": "agent-translator-02"})
    print("stored; qualified =", qualified)
except VotingError as e:
    print("rejected:", e.message)

submit_vote generates a vote_id unless you pass one, and it fills in the two placeholder fields the server requires.

docs.title: 6.5 Waiting for the result
docs.text:
report = client.wait_for_result(task_id, interval_seconds=10, timeout_seconds=3600)
print(report["winners"], report["post_award_payload"])

To see progress while voting is open, use get_bundle(task_id)["votes"], or the WebSocket live stream (§3.6).

docs.title: 6.6 Receiving invitations
docs.text:
The listener is any object with an on_voting_invite(event) method:

class Voter:
    def __init__(self, client, subject_id):
        self.client = client
        self.subject_id = subject_id

    def on_voting_invite(self, event):
        info = event["event_data"]["voting_info"]
        choice = next(iter(info["voting_options_map"]))   # replace with real logic
        self.client.submit_vote(info["social_task_id"], self.subject_id,
                                {"selected_option": choice})


invite_client = VotingClient(submission_url, intake_url, query_url)   # own client for this thread
listener = InviteListener("redis://org-redis:6379/0", "agent-reviewer-01",
                          Voter(invite_client, "agent-reviewer-01"))
listener.start()
# ...
listener.stop(timeout=5)

docs.title: 6.7 Errors
docs.text:
All HTTP failures and transport failures raise VotingError.

status_code Meaning Typical cause 400 Rejected Every vote rejection (§3.4), a bad task payload, an unknown task ID on the query server 500 Server error Missing nested key in a create request, database failure None No HTTP response Connection refused, DNS failure, timeout

The vote-intake and query servers return 400 for everything, so use e.message to tell the cases apart. A disqualified vote is not an error: submit_vote returns False.

The client does not retry. Retrying a rejected vote is pointless, because duplicate votes are refused.

docs.title: 6.8 Thread safety
docs.text: VotingClient wraps a single requests.Session, which is not guaranteed to be thread-safe. Give each thread its own client. In particular, give InviteListener's callback a separate client from your main thread, as in §6.6.

docs.title: 6.9 Limitations
docs.text:
• Generic queries are not wrapped. POST /generic-query currently fails on any non-empty result (§1.5 gap 7).
  • There is no task discovery. Subjects learn about tasks through invitations or out of band. There is no tag search like the bidding system's GET /bid-jobs/by-tags.
  • NATS is not wrapped. For NATS vote submission or result notifications, use nats-py directly (§5.3, §5.4).
  • Invitations can be missed. InviteListener only receives messages published while it is subscribed (§5.1).

docs.title: 7. Using the system in the agent SDK
docs.text:
This page shows how an agent built on the agents SDK (services/agents/libs/agents-sdk) takes part in voting, using the client from §6. It covers the two things an agent does:

  1. Vote when invited. The agent subscribes to its own Redis channel and casts a vote when a voting_invite arrives (§5.2).
  2. Act on a win. The agent learns that it won and reads the post-award payload (§5.4).

The voting system does not use the delegate service, so neither path goes through the SDK's task queue or on_data. Both run on background threads that the agent starts itself.

The worked example in §7.6 is a peer election: a group of agents elects one of themselves. Each agent is both a voter (org_ids) and an option (a voting_options_map key). Today this is the configuration in which invitations reach the voters (§1.5 gap 5).

docs.title: 7.1 How the SDK runs an agent
docs.text:
From the SDK source:

  • An agent is a class with this shape:

python class MyAgent: def __init__(self, subject, context: Context) -> None: ... def on_preprocess(self, task: AgentTask) -> Optional[List[AgentTask]]: ... def on_data(self, task: AgentTask) -> AgentResult: ...

  • The file ends with main(MyAgent). main reads SUBJECT_ID, loads the subject from SUBJECT_DB_URL, builds an AgentExecutor, and starts a Redis worker that reads tasks from REDIS_STREAM and calls on_data one at a time.
  • context.subject_id is this subject's ID. Use it as submitter_subject_id, and as the Redis channel and NATS subject to listen on.

The SDK's REDIS_URL is the agent's task queue. The voting system publishes invitations on the organisation's Redis (ORG_REDIS_URL on the voting side). These can be the same server or different servers. Configure them separately.

docs.title: 7.2 Adding the client to the SDK
docs.text:
Save the client from §6.2 into the SDK's core package:

services/agents/libs/agents-sdk/core/voting_client.py

from core.voting_client import VotingClient, VotingError, InviteListener

requests and redis are already in the SDK's requirements.txt. Add nats-py only if you use NATS for result notifications (§7.4).

docs.title: 7.3 Pattern A: voting when invited
docs.text:
Start an InviteListener on context.subject_id in __init__. Its thread calls on_voting_invite for each invitation:

def on_voting_invite(self, event: dict) -> None:
    info = event["event_data"]["voting_info"]
    task_id = info["social_task_id"]
    choice = self._choose(info, event["event_data"].get("custom_data", {}))
    try:
        qualified = self._invite_client.submit_vote(
            task_id, self.subject_id, {"selected_option": choice})
        log.info("Voted %s on %s (qualified=%s)", choice, task_id, qualified)
        self._watch(task_id)
    except VotingError as e:
        log.info("Vote refused on %s: %s", task_id, e.message)

Timing matters: the invitation is published before the task's status changes to "started" (§5.2). A vote sent immediately can be rejected with Voting task is not active yet. Retry that one message a few times with a short delay (§7.6 does this).

The listener must be subscribed when the task starts. An agent that boots after scheduled_time misses the invitation (§5.1).

docs.title: 7.4 Pattern B: learning the result
docs.text:
There are two options:

  • Poll (no extra dependency). For each task the agent voted in, poll GET /get-status/<id> on a background thread until it returns "complete", then read the report. Every voter learns the outcome this way, not just the winners. §7.6 uses this.
  • NATS (winners only). Subscribe to context.subject_id on the organisation's NATS, and handle voting_result events (§5.4). This needs nats-py and an asyncio loop on its own thread.

Either way, do not block on_data waiting for a vote to finish. The SDK processes queued tasks one at a time, and a vote can take minutes or hours.

docs.title: 7.5 Threads and clients
docs.text:
Three threads may touch the voting system:

  • the invite listener thread, which runs on_voting_invite
  • the result watcher thread, which polls for status
  • the SDK's Redis worker thread, if on_data creates tasks

Give each thread its own VotingClient (§6.8). Build all of them, and set every attribute the callbacks use, before you start the listener, because an invitation can arrive at once.

docs.title: 7.6 Worked example
docs.text:
A complete agent file for a peer election. Save it as voting_agent.py next to the SDK's other sample agents. Replace _choose with your own decision logic.

# voting_agent.py
import logging
import os
import threading
import time
from typing import Dict, Set

from core.agent_executor import AgentTask, AgentResult, Context
from core.main import main
from core.voting_client import VotingClient, VotingError, InviteListener

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def _client() -> VotingClient:
    return VotingClient(
        submission_url=os.getenv("VOTING_SUBMISSION_URL", ""),
        intake_url=os.environ["VOTING_INTAKE_URL"],
        query_url=os.environ["VOTING_QUERY_URL"],
    )


class VotingAgent:

    def __init__(self, subject, context: Context) -> None:
        self.subject = subject
        self.context = context
        self.subject_id = context.subject_id

        # One client per thread.
        self._invite_client = _client()   # invite listener thread
        self._watch_client = _client()    # result watcher thread

        self._watching: Set[str] = set()
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._poll_seconds = float(os.getenv("VOTING_RESULT_POLL_SECONDS", "15"))

        # Everything the callbacks use is set; now start the threads.
        self._watcher = threading.Thread(target=self._watch_loop, daemon=True,
                                         name="voting-results")
        self._watcher.start()
        self._listener = InviteListener(os.environ["VOTING_REDIS_URL"],
                                        self.subject_id, self)
        self._listener.start()

    # ---- pattern A: invitations (listener thread) ----

    def on_voting_invite(self, event: Dict) -> None:
        info = event["event_data"]["voting_info"]
        task_id = info["social_task_id"]
        choice = self._choose(info, event["event_data"].get("custom_data", {}))

        for attempt in range(5):
            try:
                qualified = self._invite_client.submit_vote(
                    task_id, self.subject_id, {"selected_option": choice})
                log.info("Voted %s on %s (qualified=%s)", choice, task_id, qualified)
                self._watch(task_id)
                return
            except VotingError as e:
                # The invite is published just before the task is marked
                # "started"; give the status update a moment to land.
                if "not active yet" in e.message and attempt < 4:
                    time.sleep(2)
                    continue
                log.info("Vote refused on %s: %s", task_id, e.message)
                return

    def _choose(self, info: Dict, custom_data: Dict) -> str:
        # Replace with real logic. Keys must match what the task's PQT and
        # choice-evaluation hooks expect.
        candidates = sorted(info["voting_options_map"])
        others = [c for c in candidates if c != self.subject_id]
        return (others or candidates)[0]

    # ---- pattern B: results (watcher thread) ----

    def _watch(self, task_id: str) -> None:
        with self._lock:
            self._watching.add(task_id)

    def _watch_loop(self) -> None:
        while True:
            time.sleep(self._poll_seconds)
            with self._lock:
                pending = list(self._watching)
            for task_id in pending:
                try:
                    if self._watch_client.get_status(task_id) != "complete":
                        continue
                    report = self._watch_client.get_report(task_id)
                except VotingError as e:
                    log.warning("Result poll failed for %s: %s", task_id, e)
                    continue
                with self._lock:
                    self._watching.discard(task_id)
                self._on_result(task_id, report)

    def _on_result(self, task_id: str, report: Dict) -> None:
        winners = report.get("winners", [])
        if self.subject_id in winners:
            log.info("Won %s: %s", task_id, report.get("post_award_payload"))
            # start whatever the post-award payload asks for
        else:
            log.info("Task %s decided: %s", task_id, winners)

    # ---- SDK task queue: unused by voting ----

    def on_preprocess(self, task: AgentTask):
        return [task]

    def on_data(self, task: AgentTask) -> AgentResult:
        return AgentResult(task_id=task.task_id, job_output={"ignored": True})


main(VotingAgent)

docs.title: 7.7 Operational notes
docs.text:
• Idempotency. Each subject can vote once per task. A repeated invitation, for example from a retried task start (§1.5 gap 8), produces Vote already submitted for this task., which the example logs and ignores.
  • Refusals are not errors. A VotingError from submit_vote means the task moved on or the vote was not allowed. It does not mean the agent is broken. A disqualified vote is not an error either.
  • Watched tasks are in memory. After a restart, the agent no longer polls tasks it voted in before. If outcomes matter across restarts, persist the task IDs, or query votes by submitter_subject_id once §1.5 gap 7 is fixed.
  • Shutdown. The SDK's main stops its Redis worker on SIGINT or SIGTERM, but it does not know about the listener or the watcher. Both are daemon threads, so the process exits without waiting for them. Call self._listener.stop(timeout=5) from a signal handler if you need a clean unsubscribe.
